  amount first; the minimum is 1 SUI.
- Call `deposit_receipt::keep` in the same PTB as the request. A TransferObjects
  command on the receipt fails, and an unconsumed receipt aborts the PTB.
- A receipt cannot be given to another account; only the requesting account can
  claim or cancel it.
- A claim in the request's epoch or in a safe-mode epoch aborts (codes 17, 15).
- funSUI does not earn yield; blastSUI does.
- The blastSUI price uses a conservative valuation at the cached rate. Always
  set `min_sui_out` and `min_blast_out`, ideally from a dev-inspect of the same
  call.
- The fee applies to every blastSUI redemption, however small or large.
- Every vault call takes the shared `Vault` mutably, so vault transactions are
  sequenced through consensus.
- After an upgrade, PTBs pinned to the old package ID abort (code 12 from
  `operational_version`).

### Q&A

**What is the difference between funSUI and blastSUI?** funSUI is always worth
exactly 1 SUI and earns nothing. blastSUI is a share of blast custody whose SUI
value grows with staking rewards, including the rewards on the SUI backing
funSUI.

**How long until my deposit becomes blastSUI?** Your SUI is staked at once and
activates at the next epoch. From then on, in any normal epoch, call
`blast_sui::vault::claim_blast_sui` with your receipt. Until you claim, your
stake keeps earning and is counted in your claim.

**Can I get my SUI back before claiming?** Yes. `deposit_receipt::cancel`
returns your principal, plus rewards once active, at any time, without touching
the vault.

**What does redeeming blastSUI cost?** `ceil(gross * redeem_fee_bps / 10,000)`
MIST, where the fee starts at 2 BPS and can never exceed 100 BPS. The fee stays
in the vault for the remaining holders.

**Is funSUI always redeemable one-to-one?** Yes: redemption returns exactly one
MIST per unit with no fee, from fun custody only. The vault checks fun custody
covers the funSUI supply after every operation; if it ever did not, the call
would abort rather than underpay.

**Which validator does the vault use, and can it change?** The staking pool set
at creation (`pool_id`). No call changes it.

**What happens if the validator leaves the active set?** The next refresh
unwinds all stake to liquid SUI and the vault becomes unwind-only: redemptions,
donations, and cancellations work; mints, deposits, and claims abort.

**Can Blast pause the vault or take user funds?** The current source has no
pause and no withdrawal path for anyone but coin holders and receipt owners.
Blast's `UpgradeAdmin` can upgrade the package until it is made immutable; check
`blast_sui::package_admin::has_upgrade_cap`.

**How do I compute the blastSUI to SUI rate?** Divide blast custody's assets
(`liquid_sui + pending_sui + active_sui`) by `blast_supply`, from the latest
event snapshot or a dev-inspected `sync`.

**Why can't blastSUI supply reach zero?** Creation sends the bootstrap shares to
`0x0`, where no one can redeem them. This removes every empty-vault edge case,
and those shares keep their pro-rata part of the vault forever.

## Shared core

> **Deployment status:** `blast_core` is not yet published on mainnet; its interface may change before publication.

### What it is

Package `blast_core` holds the money building blocks every Blast launch product shares, each
defined once: a basis-points unit and its exact apportionment, outright or vested payouts, the LP-fee split, the ledger that holds Blast's fees and pays the partner's cut,
the one treasury address, Merkle proofs, and the sealed values that carry a sale's liquidity to its
venue and prove a sale's ownership to its vault. It holds no user funds of its own. Products and
vaults embed its values and call it; integrators read its events and build PTBs that pass its
values between product and venue calls.

### Units and payouts

- `blast_core::bps::Bps` is a rate from 0 to 10,000 basis points; `blast_core::bps::new` aborts
  above 10,000. `blast_core::bps::apply_up` applies it rounding up.
- `blast_core::bps::apportion` splits an amount over rates that sum to exactly 10,000 by largest
  remainder: every part takes its floor, an optional named part takes its ceiling, and the
  leftover units go one each to the largest remaining remainders, earlier parts first. The parts
  always sum to the amount.
- Every launch package uses one basis-points denominator, `blast_core::constants::basis_points_denominator`
  (10,000), and one cap on Blast's share of LP fees, `blast_core::constants::max_lp_fee_bps`
  (3,000 per asset). The bounds core's constructors enforce are public too:
  `blast_core::constants::max_routes` (20 routes per fee split) and
  `blast_core::constants::max_vesting_duration_ms` (2^63 ms). All four are public compile-time
  macros.
- A `payout::Recipient`, built with `payout::recipient`, is a nonzero destination address and
  optional `payout::VestingTerms` (from `payout::vesting_terms`); the zero address aborts.
  `payout::pay_or_vest` pays an amount to a recipient as a coin or, when it vests, locks the amount
  in an irrevocable, shared `blast_fun_linear_vesting::Vesting` schedule that starts at the payout
  and returns its ID. A zero amount sends and locks nothing. Each product keeps its own recipient
  lists and shares. `payout::destination` and `payout::recipient_vesting_terms` (called as
  `recipient.vesting_terms()`) read a recipient; `payout::cliff_delay_ms`,
  `payout::period_duration_ms`, and `payout::periods` read its terms.

### Fee splits

`fee_split::FeeSplit` is a list of up to 20 routes summing to 10,000. Each route has a positive
share and a `fee_split::Destination`: an address, the vault's owner, auto-LP, holder rewards, or
burn. No address and no special kind appears twice. `fee_split::apportion` divides one collection
across the routes in order.

### Protocol fees, partners, and the treasury

`protocol_fees::Ledger` holds Blast's Meme, Quote, and SUI fees for one launch, presale, or vault.
Only the module that owns it can create it, under its package witness, and every payment event
names that witness type, so a payment's origin is attributable.
`protocol_fees::take_cut` moves Blast's rounded-up cut of a fee into it. A ledger is bound at
creation to the partner its sale named, or to none. `protocol_fees::pay` pays everything to the
treasury and aborts when a partner is bound; `protocol_fees::pay_with_partner` first pays that
partner its cut of each asset through `blast_partners::blast_partners::pay`, then the treasury the
rest. Both emit `blast_core_events::ProtocolFeesPaid`; an empty ledger sends and emits nothing. Products expose these payouts as calls anyone
may make. `protocol_fees::balances`, `protocol_fees::package_witness`, `protocol_fees::origin`, and
`protocol_fees::partner_id` read a ledger. `protocol_fees::destroy` deletes one that holds nothing
and aborts while any fee is held, so its owner pays it out first.

`blast_treasury::Treasury` is a shared singleton holding the address Blast's fees go to. A Blast
admin with `blast_domain::TreasuryAdmin` schedules a new address with
`blast_treasury::schedule_destination`; anyone applies it with `blast_treasury::apply_destination`
once its notice has passed (48 hours from publication); a Blast admin with
`blast_domain::CancelAdmin` cancels it with `blast_treasury::cancel_destination`. Read the current
address with `blast_treasury::destination`, the notice the next change waits with
`blast_treasury::delay_ms`, and a scheduled change, as a `delayed::Proposal<address>`, with
`blast_treasury::pending_destination`. `blast_treasury::is_destination_ready` takes the `Clock` and
returns whether `blast_treasury::apply_destination` would succeed now: a change is scheduled, the
clock reads its `ready_at_ms` or later, and the clock plus its next notice still fits in a `u64`;
it returns false with nothing scheduled, before `ready_at_ms`, and after a cancel or an apply. The
treasury is never deleted: every ledger pays through it.

### Migration hand-off and owner proof

- Before a sale's supply is minted, its venue prepares the coin and returns a
  `migration::VenueTicket` for the sale's exact Meme and Quote pair, sealed by the venue's witness
  (`migration::issue_ticket`), so a ticket cannot start a sale of another coin or Quote. The venue
  keeps the pair's pool tier. The product's creation call redeems the ticket with `migration::redeem_ticket`
  and stores the venue.
- `migration::VaultTerms` are a vault's terms: the sale, the package witness that sealed them, the fee
  split, Blast's LP-fee shares, the partner, and whether residuals go to Blast or the owner. Only
  `migration::vault_terms`, under the issuing package's witness, builds them. It aborts when either of Blast's LP-fee shares exceeds 3,000 basis
  points, so every sealed term is within the cap.
- At migration the product creates a `migration::Migration` with `migration::new`, sealed by its own witness, holding the
  pool's Meme and Quote and terms the same package witness sealed. Only the stored venue can consume it,
  with `migration::redeem`; any other venue aborts.
- `owner_proof::OwnerProof` is a product's sealed statement that the caller holds the sale's
  creator authority, issued with `owner_proof::new`. A vault consumes it with
  `owner_proof::assert_terms`, which aborts unless it names
  the vault's package witness and sale.

None of these values can be dropped, copied, or stored, so the PTB that creates one must consume it.

Readers never consume them. `migration::ticket_venue` (called as `ticket.venue()`) reads a ticket's
venue. `migration::venue`, `migration::balances` (the Meme and Quote amounts), and
`migration::terms` read a migration; only `migration::redeem` releases its balances, and a copy of
its terms authorizes nothing, since an admitted venue never takes terms from its caller and each
sale has one vault. `migration::origin`, `migration::package_witness`, `migration::fee_split`,
`migration::protocol_bps`, `migration::partner_id`, and `migration::residuals` read terms;
`migration::is_protocol` and `migration::is_owner` read the `migration::ResidualPolicy` it
returns. `owner_proof::package_witness` and `owner_proof::origin` read
a proof.

### Pool seed price

`migration::sqrt_price_x64` derives the price a concentrated-liquidity venue (Cetus or Bluefin)
seeds a migrated pool at, from the migration's atomic Meme and Quote amounts:
`floor(sqrt(B / A) * 2^64)`, where B / A is Quote / Meme when Meme is coin A and Meme / Quote
otherwise. Display decimals never enter it, and the divisor amount must be positive.
`migration::is_seedable_price` says whether both venues can seed a full-range pool at that price:
it must lie within half of their shared sqrt-price range (from 2 x 4,295,048,016 to
79,226,673,515,401,279,992,447,579,055 / 2). A product uses it to refuse a sale that could never
migrate. Both are pure reads anyone may call.

### Merkle proofs

`blast_core::merkle::verify` checks a positional Blake2b-256 proof of a leaf digest at an index. Leaves hash
as `blake2b256(0x00 || domain || payload)` with `blast_core::merkle::leaf`, where each tree's
purpose names its own domain string; internal nodes hash as `blake2b256(0x01 || left || right)`;
an odd node at any level is its own sibling. Malformed roots, digests, or siblings,
an empty tree, an index outside it, or a proof of the wrong depth return false instead of aborting.

### Roles

`blast_domain` declares Blast's product roles for the shared ACL: `TreasuryAdmin`, `FeeAdmin`,
`ListingAdmin`, `VenueAdmin`, `RewardsAdmin`, `BuybackAdmin`, `CreatorAdmin`,
`ClaimSignerAdmin`, and `CancelAdmin`. Only Blast admins hold them.

### Errors

Every abort is a small integer from the package's numeric registry; the reference lists each code.
The abort names the module that raised it.

## Vault

> **Deployment status:** `blast_vault` is not yet published on mainnet; its interface may change before publication.

### What it is

Package `blast_vault` holds the one LP vault every Blast sale migrates into. A vault keeps a
venue's liquidity position with no removal path, so the liquidity is locked for good. It splits
every LP-fee collection: Blast's share first, then the sale's fee split across the owner, auto-LP,
holder rewards, burn, and address routes. It also pays holder-reward rounds by Merkle proof. Only
an admitted venue's code can create a vault or move its fees, and only from terms an admitted
package witness sealed; integrators reach a vault through the
venue's calls, and call the owner, round, and payout functions on it directly.

### Objects and authority

- `blast_vault_package::VaultRegistry` (shared singleton) lists the admitted witness types: the
  venues that may create vaults and the issuers whose sealed terms they may use (the launchpad's
  and the presale's package witnesses). A witness is admitted by its type, which only its own module
  can construct. A venue obtains terms only from `blast_core::migration::redeem`; it never accepts
  terms from its caller.
- `blast_vault::vault::Vault<Meme, Quote>` (shared, one per migrated sale) holds the position under
  the venue's key, the terms the sale sealed (`blast_core::migration::VaultTerms`), the fee split
  and Blast's share, each behind a notice, and the owner, auto-LP, holder-reward, and burn
  balances.
- `blast_vault::holder_rewards::Round<Meme, Quote>` (shared, one per published round) holds one
  round's holder budget, its Merkle root, the claimed-leaf bitmap, and an optional gas reserve.
- `blast_admin::package_version::PackageVersion<BLAST_VAULT_PACKAGE>` (shared) gates every call by
  code version and holds the admin pause bit.
- Owner authority is a `blast_core::owner_proof::OwnerProof` that the sale's product issues to its
  creator-authority holder in the same PTB. A vault accepts it only for its own sale and package
  witness.

Blast admins hold these roles: `VenueAdmin` admits and removes venue and package witnesses; `FeeAdmin` changes Blast's
per-vault share; `RewardsAdmin` schedules rounds and settles gas reserves; `BuybackAdmin` spends
the burn route's Quote on buybacks; `CancelAdmin` cancels any pending change.

### Lifecycle

1. A venue creates the vault with `blast_vault::vault::new`, unshared, from terms the sale sealed.
   It aborts unless the venue's witness and the terms' sealing witness are both admitted. Blast's
   share is at most 3,000 basis points per asset because `migration::vault_terms` refuses to seal
   more.
2. The venue attaches its position and shares the vault with
   `blast_vault::vault::share_with_position`, which settles the migration residuals and emits
   `blast_vault_events::VaultCreated`.
3. Each fee collection through the venue calls `blast_vault::vault::split_fees`.
4. Holder-reward rounds are scheduled, published, claimed, and closed (see Flows).

A vault never closes; its position cannot be removed.

### Flows

#### Claim the owner's balances

1. Call the sale product's owner-proof function to get an `OwnerProof` (cap holder: the sale's
   creator authority).
2. Call `blast_vault::vault::claim_owner_balances` with the vault (shared), the proof, and the
   package version. It returns a `Coin<Meme>` and a `Coin<Quote>` holding every owner fee and
   owner residual, and emits `blast_vault_events::OwnerBalancesClaimed`. Transfer or use both coins
   in the same PTB.

#### Change the fee split (owner)

1. Get an `OwnerProof`, then call `blast_vault::vault::schedule_fee_split` with the proposed
   `blast_core::fee_split::FeeSplit` and the `Clock` (`0x6`). It is ready after a fixed 48-hour
   notice.
2. Once ready, the venue settles fees under the current split and applies the new one with
   `blast_vault::vault::apply_fee_split`, so every fee follows the split it accrued under. Integrators
   check readiness with `blast_vault::vault::assert_fee_split_ready`.
3. The owner may cancel with `blast_vault::vault::cancel_fee_split`, even once ready.

#### Pay Blast's partnered fees

When the sale named a partner, Blast's cut is held in the vault. Anyone calls
`blast_vault::vault::pay_protocol_fees_with_partner` with the vault, the package version, the
treasury, and the partner (all shared). The partner receives its cut of each asset, the treasury the
rest, and `blast_core::blast_core_events::ProtocolFeesPaid` is emitted. Without a partner, Blast's
cut is paid to the treasury during each collection.

#### Claim a holder reward

1. Read the round's leaf for your address from Blast's published allocation: the index, the
   beneficiary, the Meme and Quote amounts, and the proof (a list of 32-byte siblings).
2. Call `blast_vault::holder_rewards::claim` with the round (shared), the package version, those
   values, and the `Clock`. Anyone may relay a claim; the coins always go to the committed
   beneficiary. It emits `blast_vault_events::RewardClaimed`.

#### Close a round

At or after its claim deadline, anyone calls `blast_vault::holder_rewards::close_round` with the
round, the package version, its vault, and the `Clock`. Every unclaimed balance and any unsettled gas
reserve returns to the vault's holder rewards, and `blast_vault_events::RoundClosed` is emitted.

#### Publish a scheduled round

Once a scheduled round's notice has passed, anyone calls
`blast_vault::holder_rewards::publish_round` with the vault, the package version, the treasury, and
the `Clock`. It reserves the round's budget from the vault, opens claims for the scheduled window,
shares the `Round`, and emits `blast_vault_events::RoundPublished`.

### Economics

- Each collection first takes Blast's share of each asset, rounded up
  (`blast_core::protocol_fees::take_cut`). The rest is apportioned over the fee split's routes by
  largest remainder (`blast_core::fee_split::apportion`), so the routes always sum to what is left.
- Address routes are paid at once. Owner, auto-LP, and holder-reward routes accrue in the vault.
  The burn route's Meme is burned when the supply is burn-only, or sent to `0x0` when it is
  fixed; its Quote is kept for buybacks.
- Migration residuals go to Blast or the owner, as the sale's terms say.
- A round's gas reserve is at most 10% of its Quote budget. It is reimbursed to the treasury once,
  measured and capped, with `blast_vault::holder_rewards::settle_gas_reserve` (Blast admin:
  `RewardsAdmin`); the rest returns to the vault at once.

### Time rules

- Witness admissions start at zero notice, so Blast lists its products and venues at launch while
  the package is still paused; Blast then raises the notice before unpausing. Afterwards each
  admission and notice change waits the applied notice. Removing a witness takes effect at once:
  a removed venue creates no more vaults, and a removed package witness's sales can no longer migrate.
- Fee-split and Blast-share changes always wait 48 hours; no call changes that notice.
- A round waits the vault's round notice, 2 hours at creation, before anyone may publish it.
- Claims are open while the clock is before the deadline; a round closes at or after it.

### Pause

The package is published fully paused. The admin pause bit stops Blast-share changes, buybacks,
round scheduling and publication, and gas settlement. It never stops venue admissions, fee
collection, owner claims, partner payouts, holder claims, round closing, or cancellations.
Unpausing with `blast_vault_package::unpause` runs only on the current version and requires a
nonzero witness admission notice and a nonzero core `blast_core::blast_treasury::Treasury` notice,
with no pending admission or change to zero; it takes the `Treasury` beside the registry.

### Upgrades and immutability

The vault is upgradeable through `blast_admin`'s generic administration and is to be made
immutable after its audit. An `UpgradeAdmin<BLAST_VAULT_PACKAGE>` schedules that with
`blast_admin::package_admin::schedule_make_immutable` and, once the 48-hour upgrade notice has
passed, executes it with `blast_vault::blast_vault_package::make_immutable` (the shared
`PackageAdmin`, the role witness, the `PackageVersion` and `Clock`). The call runs only on the
current vault version (code 9 from `blast_admin::package_version` otherwise) and then destroys
the `UpgradeCap`; no later upgrade or repair is possible.

### Reading state

- Find a sale's vault without an indexer: its object ID is derived from the shared
  `blast_vault_package::VaultRegistry` and the key `blast_vault::vault::VaultKey { package_witness, origin }`,
  whose BCS is the sealing package witness's type name as a length-prefixed `String` (ULEB128
  length, then the ASCII name, with the original package ID written without `0x`) followed by the
  sale's 32-byte ID: `0x2::dynamic_field::hash_type_and_key(registry_id,
  0x2::derived_object::DerivedObjectKey<blast_vault::vault::VaultKey>, bcs(key))`. The launchpad's
  sealing package witness is `blast_fun::blast_fun::PackageWitness` and the presale's
  `blast_presale::blast_presale_package::PackageWitness`. Each sale has exactly one vault; a
  second `blast_vault::vault::new` for the same terms aborts in `sui::derived_object`.

- `blast_vault::vault::pool_id`: the pool the vault's position belongs to.
- The venue's positions are dynamic object fields of the vault, under the venue's
  `PositionKey` and, once auto-LP has opened one, `AutoLpPositionKey`; only the venue's own code
  can borrow them, so read them as object fields.
- Events carry every balance change; index `FeesCollected` for per-route amounts.

### Events

- `blast_vault_events::VaultCreated`: vault, pool, position, liquidity, terms, and residuals.
- `blast_vault_events::FeesCollected`: gross amounts, Blast's cut, and each route's amounts, in
  route order.
- `blast_vault_events::AutoLpPositionOpened`, `blast_vault_events::AutoLiquidityAdded`: auto-LP.
- `blast_vault_events::BuybackBurned`: Quote spent and Meme burned. The vault measures both from
  the buyback receipt, as it measures `AutoLiquidityAdded` from the auto-LP receipt.
- Burned Meme leaves the supply when the Meme `Currency` is burn-only; when its supply is fixed
  it is sent to `0x0` instead. Both supply states are final, so an indexer reads the
  currency's supply state once to tell the two apart.
- `blast_vault_events::OwnerBalancesClaimed`: the owner's payout.
- `blast_vault_events::RoundPublished`, `blast_vault_events::RewardClaimed`,
  `blast_vault_events::GasReserveSettled`, `blast_vault_events::RoundClosed`: rounds.

### Aborts

- Vault creation: `unadmitted_venue`, then `unadmitted_package_witness`. Scheduling Blast's share above
  3,000 basis points per asset aborts with `invalid_protocol_bps`.
- A venue's buyback or auto-LP return: `wrong_vault` for another vault's receipt,
  `returned_exceeds_taken` when it returns more than it took.
- Owner claim with nothing accrued: `nothing_to_claim`. A proof for another sale or package
  aborts in `blast_core::owner_proof`.
- Holder claim: `claims_closed` past the deadline, `invalid_index`, `already_claimed`,
  `invalid_beneficiary` for `0x0`, `empty_claim` for zero amounts, and `invalid_proof` when any
  leaf value or the proof is wrong.
- Closing a round early: `claims_still_open`; with another vault: `wrong_vault`.
- Publishing: the scheduled round's notice must have passed, the treasury must still be the one it
  expected (`treasury_changed`), and the vault must still hold its budget
  (`insufficient_budget`).

### Pitfalls

- The coins from an owner claim must be consumed in the same PTB.
- An `OwnerProof` cannot be stored or dropped; create it in the PTB that uses it.
- A claim relayed by anyone still pays the beneficiary in the leaf, never the relayer.
- A leaf's beneficiary must be an account. A claim pays by coin transfer, so a beneficiary that is
  an object (a pool, a vesting schedule, another vault) could never receive it, and the claimed
  leaf never returns to the vault. Blast's allocation leaves object-held balances out; nothing on
  chain tells the two apart.

### Q&A

**Can anyone withdraw the liquidity?** No. The position is held under the venue's key with no
removal path; only the venue's code can borrow it to collect fees or add auto-LP.

**Who receives the burn route's Meme?** Nobody: it is burned when the supply is burn-only, or sent
to `0x0` when it is fixed.

**Do claims stop when Blast pauses the vault package?** No. Holder claims, owner claims, fee
collection, and round closing never pause.

**What happens to unclaimed rewards?** At the deadline anyone closes the round and they return to
the vault's holder rewards for later rounds.

**Can Blast change its share?** Yes, up to 3,000 basis points per asset, after a fixed 48-hour
notice and only for fees collected afterwards.

## Administration

> **Deployment status:** `blast_admin` is not yet published on mainnet; its interface may change before publication.

### What it is

Package `blast_admin` is Blast's administration layer. It holds one shared
access-control list (ACL) for every Blast package, with one cold root capability
and a Table of administrator capabilities with no inline cardinality limit. Each
administrator holds roles, and a role is a Move type that a consumer package
declares, so a role from one package can never act in another. The package also
provides the delayed-notice primitives Blast's settings embed, and one generic
package administration that every upgradeable Blast package uses: a shared
`PackageVersion<OTW>` that rejects calls into outdated bytecode and holds the
package's pause bits, and a shared `PackageAdmin<OTW>` that seals the package's
`Publisher` and `UpgradeCap` so upgrades happen only through role-gated,
48-hour-notice calls and only the package itself can borrow its `Publisher`. No package can build a second version or PackageAdmin:
both are created only by `blast_admin::package_admin::wrap` from the package's
own publication. Blast publishes `blast_admin` immutable (its `UpgradeCap` is
destroyed in the publish transaction), so none of these rules can change.

### Objects and authority

| Object | Kind | Held by | Authorizes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `blast_acl::ACL` | shared singleton, created once in `init` | nobody | stores the root cap ID, every live `AdminCap` ID with its roles, and the pending root transfer |
| `blast_acl::SuperAdminCap` | owned, `key` only (cannot be transferred or wrapped by anyone) | Blast's cold root: `init` delivers it to the `blast_acl_root` address in `Move.toml`, not the publisher | grant and revoke admins and roles; start and cancel a root transfer |
| `blast_acl::AdminCap` | owned, `key, store` (transferable, wrappable) | a Blast operator | nothing by itself; `blast_acl::sign_in` turns it into a role witness |
| `blast_acl::AdminWitness<Role>` | transaction-local value, `drop` only | the PTB that signed in | the one role `Role` in every consumer call that takes `&AdminWitness<Role>` |
| `package_version::Publication<OTW>` | owned, `key` only | the publisher, from the package's `init` until wrap | nothing but the one wrap of package `OTW` |
| `package_version::PackageVersion<OTW>` | shared, `key` only, created at wrap | nobody | the version and pause bits package `OTW`'s operations check |
| `blast_admin::package_admin::PackageAdmin<OTW>` | shared, `key` only, created at wrap | nobody | package `OTW`'s sealed `Publisher` (borrowed only by `OTW` itself) and `UpgradeCap`, and its delayed upgrade decisions |

`OTW` is the package's one-time witness type, named as in the framework's
`sui::package::claim<OTW: drop>`, for example the vault's
`blast_vault::blast_vault_package::BLAST_VAULT_PACKAGE`.

`ACL` fields: `super_admin_cap_id` (the one root cap that works), `admins` (a
map from `AdminCap` ID to a set of role type names), and `super_admin_transfer`
(a `delayed_action::DelayedAction<blast_acl::SuperAdminTransfer, address>` with a
fixed seven-day notice; see "Delayed values, actions, sets and maps").

Root powers are narrow: membership, roles, and its own delayed transfer. Root
cannot sign in to any role and cannot call any consumer function. Every
operational action needs an `AdminCap` holding the right role.

### Roles

A role is an ability-free struct. The ACL stores its type name with defining
IDs and type arguments: the address of the package that first declared it, then
module, struct and any type arguments. Same-named roles in different packages,
or with different type arguments, are different roles.

| Declared in | Roles | Used by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `blast_admin::package_admin` | `blast_admin::package_admin::UpgradeAdmin<OTW>` (schedule, authorize and commit upgrades, schedule and execute immutability, change the upgrade notice), `blast_admin::package_admin::PauseAdmin<OTW>` (set pause bits), `blast_admin::package_admin::UnpauseAdmin<OTW>` (clear pause bits through the package's own unpause), `blast_admin::package_admin::CancelAdmin<OTW>` (cancel the pending upgrade action or notice change) | every upgradeable package, typed by its one-time witness `OTW` |
| `blast_core::blast_domain` | `blast_domain::TreasuryAdmin`, `blast_domain::FeeAdmin`, `blast_domain::ListingAdmin`, `blast_domain::VenueAdmin`, `blast_domain::RewardsAdmin`, `blast_domain::BuybackAdmin`, `blast_domain::CreatorAdmin`, `blast_domain::ClaimSignerAdmin`, `blast_domain::CancelAdmin` | the launch products, the vault and the migrators |
| `blast_partners` | `blast_partners::blast_partners::PartnerAdmin` (register partners, schedule shares and caps) | partners |
| `blast_boosts_core` | `blast_boosts_core::blast_boosts_core::VaultIssuer`, `blast_boosts_core::blast_boosts_core::RiskAdmin`, `blast_boosts_core::blast_boosts_core::ShutdownAdmin`, `blast_boosts_core::blast_boosts_core::UpgradeAdmin` | Boosts |

Two `CancelAdmin` roles exist by design: `blast_admin::package_admin::CancelAdmin<OTW>`
cancels one package's upgrade actions; `blast_domain::CancelAdmin` cancels product
proposals.

### Lifecycle

**Administrator.** `blast_acl::grant_admin` mints a roleless `AdminCap` to a
recipient. `blast_acl::grant_role` and `blast_acl::revoke_role` add or remove
one role at a time. `blast_acl::revoke_admin` removes the cap's entry and all
its roles without needing the cap; the object remains but signs in to nothing.
`blast_acl::destroy_admin_cap` lets the holder delete its cap, live or revoked.
Transferring an `AdminCap` moves its roles with it, because the ACL tracks caps
by ID.

**Root transfer.** No nomination → nominated (waiting seven days) → ready →
accepted. Root nominates with `blast_acl::begin_super_admin_transfer`; a new
nomination replaces the old one and restarts the delay. Root can cancel at any
time with `blast_acl::cancel_super_admin_transfer`, even after the delay. After
seven days the nominee calls `blast_acl::accept_super_admin_transfer`, which
mints a new `SuperAdminCap` to the nominee and makes the old one inert. The old
holder may then delete it with `blast_acl::destroy_retired_super_admin_cap`.

**Package.** Published (owned `Publication<OTW>`) → wrapped (shared
`PackageAdmin<OTW>` and `PackageVersion<OTW>`, version 1, every defined bit
paused) → unpaused by the package's own `unpause` → upgraded any number of
times (each commit advances the version by exactly one) → optionally
immutable. The cap's upgrade policy is never narrowed: it stays compatible (0,
the policy after a plain publish) until `blast_admin::package_admin::make_immutable`
destroys it, the one terminal upgrade action. Narrowing is deliberately absent:
under an additive or dependency-only policy a release cannot change existing
modules, so it could not compile the next version, and after
`blast_admin::package_admin::commit_upgrade_and_advance` every version-gated call
would abort forever.

### Flows

Integrators cannot call admin functions. These flows explain what Blast does and
what each transaction leaves on chain.

#### Use a role in an admin PTB (Blast admin)

1. `blast_acl::sign_in` with type argument `Role` (the role's full type), the
   shared `ACL` by immutable reference, and the operator's owned `AdminCap` by
   reference. It aborts unless the cap is live and holds `Role`. It returns an
   `AdminWitness<Role>`.
2. Pass the witness by reference to each consumer call that names that role, in
   the same PTB, for example `blast_admin::package_admin::pause` with
   `AdminWitness<blast_admin::package_admin::PauseAdmin<OTW>>`. One witness serves
   any number of calls of the same role.
3. A PTB that needs two roles signs in twice. The witness drops at the end of
   the transaction; it cannot be stored or sent.

#### Grant or remove an administrator (root)

1. `blast_acl::grant_admin` with the shared `ACL`, the owned `SuperAdminCap`,
   and the recipient. Emits `AdminGranted`; the new cap's ID is in the event.
2. `blast_acl::grant_role` with type argument `Role` and the cap ID. Emits
   `AdminRoleGranted`. Repeat per role.
3. To remove: `blast_acl::revoke_role` (one role, emits `AdminRoleRevoked`) or
   `blast_acl::revoke_admin` (the whole cap, emits `AdminRevoked` with the roles
   it held).

#### Transfer root (root, then nominee)

1. Root calls `blast_acl::begin_super_admin_transfer` with the recipient and
   `Clock` at `0x6`. Emits `delayed_action::ActionScheduled<blast_acl::SuperAdminTransfer, address>`
   with the nominee and `ready_at_ms` (and `delayed_action::ActionCancelled` first
   for a replaced nominee).
2. At or after `ready_at_ms`, the nominee's address calls
   `blast_acl::accept_super_admin_transfer` with the `ACL` and `Clock`. Emits
   `delayed_action::ActionApplied` and `SuperAdminTransferred` with the old and new
   cap IDs.
3. The old holder may call `blast_acl::destroy_retired_super_admin_cap`. Emits
   `SuperAdminCapDestroyed`.

#### Publish and wrap a package (publisher)

1. The package's `init` calls `package_version::new_publication` with its
   one-time witness by value, the bits it defines (`valid_pause_bits`; zero
   defines none) and a second type argument, the package's package witness: a
   struct of that package, other than its OTW, whose value only the package's
   own code constructs and never returns or stores. It is the one type that
   clears the package's pause bits and borrows its `Publisher`. The publication stores that exact type (with
   defining IDs) and aborts with code 24 for a primitive, the OTW itself, or a
   type from another package. It then claims the package's `Publisher`, which the
   framework allows only with a genuine one-time witness, and
   `package_version::keep` transfers the `Publication<OTW>` to the publisher.
2. In the publication PTB the publisher calls
   `blast_admin::package_admin::wrap` with that `Publication` and the fresh
   `UpgradeCap`. Wrap aborts with code 10 unless the cap belongs to the OTW's
   package and was never upgraded (UpgradeCap version 1, no outstanding ticket). It
   seals both capabilities in the new `PackageAdmin<OTW>` with a 48-hour upgrade
   notice (emits `PackageAdminCreated`) and shares it beside the
   `PackageVersion<OTW>` with every defined bit paused.

#### Upgrade a package (Blast admin)

1. Sign in with `UpgradeAdmin<OTW>` and call
   `blast_admin::package_admin::schedule_upgrade` with the shared
   `PackageAdmin<OTW>`, the witness, the 32-byte digest and `Clock`. It replaces
   any pending action or notice change and is ready after the applied notice.
   It aborts with code 12 once the package is immutable and with code 11 for a
   digest that is not 32 bytes.
2. After the notice, in one PTB: sign in again;
   `blast_admin::package_admin::authorize_upgrade` with the same digest and
   `Clock` consumes the ready action (code 22 when it is not the upgrade of that
   digest) and returns an `UpgradeTicket` under the cap's current policy (emits
   `UpgradeAuthorized`); the native `Upgrade` command returns an
   `UpgradeReceipt`; `blast_admin::package_admin::commit_upgrade_and_advance`
   takes the `PackageAdmin<OTW>`, the witness, the `PackageVersion<OTW>` by mutable
   reference, and the receipt. It commits the receipt into the sealed cap and
   advances the stored version by one in the same call (emits
   `UpgradeCommitted` and `VersionAdvanced`). Any failure rolls back
   the whole upgrade.

From the next transaction, calls into the previous bytecode abort with code 9
and the new bytecode, which must compile the next version, is the only one
that works. Because `blast_admin` is immutable, these administration calls check
no consumer version: a package whose new bytecode compiled the wrong
version can still schedule and install a repair.

`blast_admin::package_admin::schedule_make_immutable` and
`blast_admin::package_admin::make_immutable` destroy the `UpgradeCap` the same
way (emits `UpgradeCapDestroyed`); the `Publisher` stays sealed. Once the cap is
destroyed, both schedule calls abort with code 12. `make_immutable` also takes
a value of the package witness and the `PackageVersion<OTW>`, and aborts with
code 26 for any other type before it consumes the action. Only the package's
own code can therefore end its upgrades. Each package that may end them wraps
the call in a thin function that first runs
`package_version::assert_current(constants::version!())`, so only its live
bytecode can: the vault does, with `blast_vault::blast_vault_package::make_immutable`.
The launchpad, presale and migrators are upgradeable and have no such wrapper
yet; one of their upgrades must add it before they can be made immutable.
`blast_admin::package_admin::schedule_upgrade_delay` proposes only a new notice,
which anyone applies with `blast_admin::package_admin::apply_upgrade_delay` once
ready; `blast_admin::package_admin::cancel_upgrade_action` (`CancelAdmin<OTW>`)
discards whatever is pending, even when ready.

#### Pause and unpause a package (Blast admin)

1. `blast_admin::package_admin::pause` with the `PackageVersion<OTW>` by mutable
   reference, the `PauseAdmin<OTW>` witness and the bits sets them at once and emits
   `blast_admin_events::Paused`.
2. Clearing goes through the package's own `unpause`, which checks the current
   version, the package's own configuration notices and the core treasury's, then calls
   `blast_admin::package_admin::clear_pause_bits` with the `PackageAdmin<OTW>`, the
   `UnpauseAdmin<OTW>` witness, a value of the package witness type pinned at
   publication, the `PackageVersion<OTW>`, and the bits. Any other type aborts with
   code 25, including every other droppable type the package defines or returns,
   so an `UnpauseAdmin<OTW>` cannot skip the package's own checks by calling
   `blast_admin` directly. It then aborts with code 23 while any upgrade notice
   still to come could be zero, and emits `blast_admin_events::Unpaused`.

Pause and unpause requests must name nonzero bits the package defines (code 19)
and must change at least one bit (code 20); the witness and notice checks come
first. `package_version::assert_not_paused` aborts with code 21 while an
operation's bit is set; it is a mask check only, so a bit the package never
defined never aborts.

#### Borrow the package's Publisher (the package's own code)

`blast_admin::package_admin::publisher` takes the shared `PackageAdmin<OTW>`, a value
of `OTW`'s package witness and the shared `PackageVersion<OTW>`, and returns
`&Publisher`: the one the `OTW` value claimed at publication. Only `OTW`'s
own modules can construct that witness, so only package `OTW` can borrow its
Publisher, for example to create a `sui::display::Display` or a transfer policy
for its own types inside one of its functions. Any other type aborts with code
26. `blast_admin::package_admin::publisher_mut` is the same call returning
`&mut Publisher`, for framework calls that take one, such as
`sui::display_registry::new_with_publisher`; it checks the same witness and
aborts with the same code 26 (`EWrongPackageWitness`). A `Publisher` has no `drop`, so neither reference
can overwrite or burn it, and the pinned framework has no call that moves a
value out from behind a mutable reference. Should a later framework add a
generic swap, only package `OTW` itself, the holder of its witness, could use it,
and the Publisher would then leave this PackageAdmin; no other caller can.

### Version

Every protected call of an upgradeable package passes its shared
`PackageVersion<OTW>` and runs `package_version::assert_current` with the
version compiled into that bytecode, which aborts with code 9 unless it
equals the stored one. The version starts at 1 at wrap and changes only in
`blast_admin::package_admin::commit_upgrade_and_advance`, by exactly one.
`VersionAdvanced<OTW>` carries `container_id` (the `PackageVersion<OTW>`
ID), `original_package_id`, and the old and new versions. Integrators pass
the version object as a shared, immutable input to every call that takes it and
must call the latest package version.

### Delayed values, actions, sets and maps

The delayed modules are a timelock in the Compound/OpenZeppelin sense: schedule,
wait the applied notice, then apply; cancellable until applied. Each module owns
one type; consumers store four:

| Type | Holds | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `delayed::Delayed<K, T>` | an applied `value`, its applied `delay_ms`, at most one `delayed::Proposal<T>` | fees, shares, treasuries, destinations, fee splits |
| `delayed_action::DelayedAction<K, A>` | an applied `delay_ms`, at most one `delayed::Proposal<delayed_action::Change<A>>` | one-shot actions: upgrades, immutability, creator-cap reassignment, holder-reward rounds, the root transfer |
| `delayed_set::DelayedSet<K, E>` | admitted `members`, an applied `delay_ms`, pending admissions with fixed deadlines (each a `delayed::PendingDelay`), at most one proposed notice | witness and venue allowlists, the launchpad's account-claim signer keys |
| `delayed_map::DelayedMap<K, E, V>` | applied values by entry `E` in a `Table`, one applied `delay_ms`, at most one pending change per entry with a fixed deadline, at most one proposed notice | keyed values such as per-coin overrides |

Every value carries an `owner` (the ID of the object that stores it) and a `key`
of type `K`. `delayed::new`, `delayed_action::new`, `delayed_set::new` and
`delayed_map::new` take the owner object's `&UID`, which only the code creating
or holding that object has, so no package can attribute a value or its events to
another package's object. Blast keys are structs without public constructors, so
only their module can produce events under them. Partition delayed events by
`owner`, then by `K`.

Rules shared by all four:

- **Old notice governs.** Every proposal is ready at its scheduling time plus the
  notice applied then. A shorter notice, zero included, waits the applied one.
- **Explicit application.** Nothing changes until `delayed::apply`,
  `delayed_action::take_action`, `delayed_set::apply_add`, `delayed_map::apply`,
  or a notice `apply_delay` consumes a ready proposal. Readiness alone changes no
  value. Reads need no Clock, except the `is_ready` and `is_delay_ready`
  predicates, which answer whether the matching apply would succeed now.
- **Cancellation until applied.** `delayed::cancel`, `delayed_action::cancel`,
  `delayed_set::cancel_add`, `delayed_map::cancel` and the notice cancels work
  even after readiness. Scheduling over a pending proposal cancels it and
  restarts the full applied notice.
- **Zero-notice bootstrap.** A notice can start at zero, so a schedule and its
  apply in one PTB act as a setter. Raising a notice from zero applies at once.
  There is no other mutation path. `delayed::is_guarded`, `delayed_action::is_guarded`,
  `delayed_set::is_guarded` and `delayed_map::is_guarded` report whether every
  change still to come waits a nonzero notice (for a set or map, also that no
  admission or entry change is pending); each package's `unpause` requires it of
  its policies and of the core treasury destination.
- **Ceiling.** No notice exceeds `delayed::max_delay_ms` (2,592,000,000 ms, 30
  days): constructors and every proposed next notice abort with code 15 above it,
  so any notice can always be changed again.
- **No-op rejection.** A `Delayed` proposal that changes neither value nor notice,
  a notice proposal equal to the applied notice, admitting a current member, and
  a map change to the entry's applied value abort with code 16.
- **Overflow.** Scheduling and application abort with code 15 when a notice exceeds
  the ceiling, or a deadline or the next notice would not fit in a `u64` millisecond
  timestamp.
- **Destruction.** `delayed::destroy`, `delayed_action::destroy`,
  `delayed_set::destroy` and `delayed_map::destroy` delete a value whose owner is
  being deleted. Each aborts with code 17 while anything is pending, so every
  proposal ends in an event, and emits its module's `Destroyed` event.
  Destroying a set or map also ends its remaining members or entries.

`Delayed`: `delayed::schedule` proposes a value and the next notice together;
`delayed::schedule_value` keeps the notice; `delayed::schedule_delay` keeps the
value. `delayed::assert_ready` checks readiness without changing anything, so an
owner can settle accrued economics under the applied value before `delayed::apply`.

`DelayedAction`: `delayed_action::schedule` proposes an action under the applied
notice; `delayed_action::schedule_delay` proposes only a notice change.
`delayed_action::take_action` returns a ready action to its owner and aborts with
code 18 when the proposal is a notice change; `delayed_action::apply_delay` does
the reverse. `delayed_action::Change` is `Action(A)` or `Delay`.

`DelayedSet`: `delayed_set::schedule_add` snapshots a member's deadline from the
applied notice; a later notice change never moves it. `delayed_set::apply_add`
admits a ready member; `delayed_set::remove` removes a member and discards its
pending admission at once (removal is never delayed). `delayed_set::SetChange` is
`Admission(E)` or `Delay`.

`DelayedMap`: `delayed_map::schedule` proposes setting an entry to a value, or
clearing it with none, and snapshots its deadline from the applied notice; a
later notice change never moves it. Clearing is a delayed change like any other.
`delayed_map::apply` sets or clears a ready entry. `delayed_map::MapChange` is
`Entry { entry, value }` or `Delay`.

#### Delayed readers

Every reader is read-only. The same name means the same concept on every type.

| Concept | `Delayed` | `DelayedAction` | `DelayedSet` | `DelayedMap` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| owner object ID, key | `delayed::owner`, `delayed::key` | `delayed_action::owner`, `delayed_action::key` | `delayed_set::owner`, `delayed_set::key` | `delayed_map::owner`, `delayed_map::key` |
| applied state | `delayed::value` | none | `delayed_set::contains`, `delayed_set::members`, `delayed_set::length` | `delayed_map::value`, `delayed_map::contains`, `delayed_map::length` |
| applied notice | `delayed::delay_ms` | `delayed_action::delay_ms` | `delayed_set::delay_ms` | `delayed_map::delay_ms` |
| pending proposal | `delayed::pending` | `delayed_action::pending`, `delayed_action::pending_action` | `delayed_set::is_pending`, `delayed_set::admission_delay`, `delayed_set::admission_ready_at_ms`, `delayed_set::pending_count` | `delayed_map::is_pending`, `delayed_map::pending`, `delayed_map::entry_ready_at_ms`, `delayed_map::pending_count` |
| ready now | `delayed::is_ready` | `delayed_action::is_ready` | `delayed_set::is_ready` (per member) | `delayed_map::is_ready` (per entry) |
| pending notice change | in `delayed::pending` | `delayed_action::pending_delay`, `delayed_action::is_delay_ready` | `delayed_set::pending_delay`, `delayed_set::is_delay_ready` | `delayed_map::pending_delay`, `delayed_map::is_delay_ready` |
| guarded | `delayed::is_guarded` | `delayed_action::is_guarded` | `delayed_set::is_guarded` | `delayed_map::is_guarded` |

Value types: `delayed::Proposal` exposes `delayed::proposal_value`,
`delayed::proposal_delay_ms` and `delayed::proposal_ready_at_ms` (also as `value`,
`delay_ms` and `ready_at_ms` on the value); `delayed::PendingDelay` exposes
`delayed::pending_delay_ms` and `delayed::pending_delay_ready_at_ms` (also as `delay_ms`
and `ready_at_ms`); `delayed_map::EntryProposal` exposes
`delayed_map::entry_proposal_value` (none clears) and
`delayed_map::entry_proposal_delay`; `delayed_action::action`,
`delayed_set::member`, `delayed_map::changed_entry` and
`delayed_map::changed_value` read a change, each none for a delay change.
`delayed_map::changed_value` returns `Option<Option<V>>`: `some(some(v))` sets
the entry to `v` and `some(none)` clears it.

The launchpad's account-claim signer keys are a `DelayedSet`: ClaimSignerAdmin's admissions wait
the set's notice, so a compromised ClaimSignerAdmin cannot sign claims without warning, and its
revocations are immediate. ACL administrator and role grants remain immediate.

### Time rules

- Root transfer delay: 604,800,000 ms (seven days), fixed in immutable code. The
  nominee may accept from the first transaction whose `Clock` reads
  `ready_at_ms` or later.
- The root transfer is a `DelayedAction` with no notice-change path. Accepting
  consumes the nomination; cancelling or replacing it discards the old nominee,
  so a replaced, cancelled, or already accepted nominee can never accept.
- Upgrade and immutability actions wait the package's upgrade notice, 172,800,000
  ms (48 hours) from wrap until an applied notice change.
- Grants, revocations, role changes and pauses take effect in the same transaction.

### Reading state

`blast_admin` is immutable and keeps a complete read-only API for every type it
defines, so a future package can explain any state on chain; off-chain readers
can also read object content over RPC, or replay events.

- ACL: `blast_acl::super_admin_cap_id` (the active root; any other
  `SuperAdminCap` is inert), `blast_acl::is_admin`, `blast_acl::has_role`,
  `blast_acl::admin_roles` (aborts with code 1 for an unknown cap),
  `blast_acl::admin_count`, `blast_acl::super_admin_transfer` (the root transfer's
  `DelayedAction`, whose `pending` holds `Action(nominee)` and its `ready_at_ms`),
  and the fixed `blast_acl::max_roles_per_admin` and
  `blast_acl::super_admin_transfer_delay_ms`. Role type-name strings use 64
  lowercase hex characters for the address, without `0x`.
- Package version: `package_version::version`, `package_version::valid_pause_bits`,
  `package_version::paused`, `package_version::is_paused` (any of the given bits
  set) and `package_version::package_witness`; a `Publication` exposes
  `package_version::publication_valid_pause_bits` and
  `package_version::publication_package_witness` and
  `package_version::publication_publisher_id`.
- Package administration: `blast_admin::package_admin::upgrade_delay_ms`,
  `blast_admin::package_admin::pending_upgrade` (read its action with
  `delayed_action::action` and the digest with
  `blast_admin::package_admin::upgrade_digest`, none for immutability),
  `blast_admin::package_admin::is_upgrade_delay_guarded`,
  `blast_admin::package_admin::has_upgrade_cap`,
  `blast_admin::package_admin::upgrade_cap_id`,
  `blast_admin::package_admin::current_package_id`,
  `blast_admin::package_admin::upgrade_cap_version` and
  `blast_admin::package_admin::upgrade_policy` (each none once immutable),
  `blast_admin::package_admin::publisher_id`, and
  `blast_admin::package_admin::initial_upgrade_delay_ms`.

`ACL`, `PackageVersion` and `PackageAdmin` are shared for the life of the
protocol and have no destructor; a `Publication` has none either, because its
one exit, wrap, keeps the Publisher in custody. `AdminCap` and a retired
`SuperAdminCap` have their destroy calls above.

### Events

All `blast_admin` events are emitted directly (no envelope). ACL, version and
PackageAdmin events come from module `blast_admin_events` and carry no ACL ID because
there is one ACL. Delayed lifecycle events come from the module that owns the
type (`delayed`, `delayed_action`, `delayed_set` or `delayed_map`), are generic in
the owner's key `K` and the value, action, member or entry types, and carry
`owner` and `key`. Each map event's `change` names its entry.

| Event | Emitted by | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `blast_admin_events::AdminGranted` | `grant_admin` | new cap ID and recipient |
| `blast_admin_events::AdminRoleGranted` / `blast_admin_events::AdminRoleRevoked` | `grant_role` / `revoke_role` | role added or removed (`role` is the type name) |
| `blast_admin_events::AdminRevoked` | `revoke_admin` | cap removed with the roles it held |
| `blast_admin_events::AdminDestroyed` | `destroy_admin_cap` | cap deleted; `was_active` and the roles it still held |
| `blast_admin_events::SuperAdminTransferred` | `accept_super_admin_transfer` | old and new root cap IDs, recipient |
| `blast_admin_events::SuperAdminCapDestroyed` | `destroy_retired_super_admin_cap` | retired root deleted |
| `blast_admin_events::PackageAdminCreated` | `blast_admin::package_admin::wrap` | `PackageAdmin<OTW>` created: Publisher, cap, package, UpgradeCap version, policy |
| `blast_admin_events::PackageVersionCreated` | `blast_admin::package_admin::wrap` | `PackageVersion<OTW>` created beside its `PackageAdmin<OTW>` (`package_admin_id`): defined and paused bits, package witness, version 1 |
| `blast_admin_events::UpgradeAuthorized` | `blast_admin::package_admin::authorize_upgrade` | the exact digest authorized, from `current_package_id` |
| `blast_admin_events::UpgradeCommitted` | `blast_admin::package_admin::commit_upgrade_and_advance` | new package ID and UpgradeCap version |
| `blast_admin_events::VersionAdvanced` | `blast_admin::package_admin::commit_upgrade_and_advance` | version bump of package `OTW` |
| `blast_admin_events::UpgradeCapDestroyed` | `blast_admin::package_admin::make_immutable` | final UpgradeCap version and policy |
| `blast_admin_events::Paused` | `blast_admin::package_admin::pause` | bits set on package `OTW`'s version and the resulting mask; the one pause event of every package |
| `blast_admin_events::Unpaused` | `blast_admin::package_admin::clear_pause_bits` | bits cleared and the resulting mask |
| `delayed::DelayedCreated` | `delayed::new` | initial value and notice |
| `delayed::DelayedScheduled` / `delayed::DelayedCancelled` | schedule, replace, cancel | proposed value, next notice, `ready_at_ms` |
| `delayed::DelayedApplied` | `delayed::apply` | previous and new value, applied notice |
| `delayed::DelayedDestroyed` | `delayed::destroy` | the setting ends |
| `delayed_action::ActionCreated` | `delayed_action::new` | initial notice |
| `delayed_action::ActionScheduled` / `delayed_action::ActionCancelled` | action or notice proposals | `change`, notice in force once applied, `ready_at_ms` |
| `delayed_action::ActionApplied` | `delayed_action::take_action`, `delayed_action::apply_delay` | `change` and the notice now applied |
| `delayed_action::ActionDestroyed` | `delayed_action::destroy` | the action slot ends |
| `delayed_set::SetCreated` | `delayed_set::new` | initial notice |
| `delayed_set::SetScheduled` / `delayed_set::SetCancelled` | admission or notice proposals; a removal cancels a pending admission | `change`, the notice an admission waits or the proposed notice, `ready_at_ms` |
| `delayed_set::SetApplied` | `delayed_set::apply_add`, `delayed_set::apply_delay` | `change` and the notice it waited or now applied |
| `delayed_set::MemberRemoved` | `delayed_set::remove` | member removed at once |
| `delayed_set::SetDestroyed` | `delayed_set::destroy` | the set and its members end |
| `delayed_map::MapCreated` | `delayed_map::new` | initial notice |
| `delayed_map::MapScheduled` / `delayed_map::MapCancelled` | entry or notice proposals | `change` (entry and value, none to clear), the notice an entry change waits or the proposed notice, `ready_at_ms` |
| `delayed_map::MapApplied` | `delayed_map::apply`, `delayed_map::apply_delay` | `change` and the notice it waited or now applied |
| `delayed_map::MapDestroyed` | `delayed_map::destroy` | the map and its entries end |

Every upgrade event names the package's `original_package_id`, except
`UpgradeAuthorized`, which names the `current_package_id` the digest upgrades
from. Replaying the ACL events in order reconstructs `ACL.admins` and every root
transfer exactly. `ACL` creation emits only the root transfer's
`delayed_action::ActionCreated`, so the first root cap's ID comes from the publish
transaction's created objects (or the first `SuperAdminTransferred`, as
`previous_super_admin_cap_id`). A proposal ends in exactly one `Applied` or
`Cancelled` event.

### Aborts

Codes are plain `u64` values raised in the `blast_admin` module named. An error a
delayed type raises in its own call is located in that type's module; readiness
and overflow checked through the shared deadline rules are located in `delayed`.

| Code | Name | Module | Cause and fix |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | `EInvalidSuperAdminCap` | `blast_acl` | the root cap is not the active one |
| 1 | `EInvalidAdminCap` | `blast_acl` | the `AdminCap` is revoked or unknown (in `sign_in`, `grant_role`, `revoke_role`, `revoke_admin`, `admin_roles`) |
| 2 | `EInvalidAdminRecipient` | `blast_acl` | `grant_admin` to `0x0` |
| 3 | `EAdminRoleCapacityReached` | `blast_acl` | the cap already holds 32 roles |
| 4 | `EAdminRoleAlreadyGranted` | `blast_acl` | the cap already holds the role |
| 5 | `EAdminRoleNotGranted` | `blast_acl` | `sign_in` or `revoke_role` for a role the cap does not hold; grant it first or use the right role type |
| 6 | `EInvalidSuperAdminRecipient` | `blast_acl` | nominee is `0x0` or the sender; or publish with `blast_acl_root` left at `0x0` |
| 7 | `ENotPendingSuperAdminRecipient` | `blast_acl` | accept from an address that is not the nominee, or with no nomination pending; checked before readiness |
| 8 | `ESuperAdminCapStillActive` | `blast_acl` | destroying the active root |
| 9 | `EVersionMismatch` | `package_version` | the call reached outdated bytecode; call the latest package version (or the upgrade did not compile the next version) |
| 10 | `EInvalidUpgradeCap` | `blast_admin::package_admin` | wrap received a cap for another package, an already upgraded cap, or one with an outstanding ticket |
| 11 | `EInvalidPackageDigest` | `blast_admin::package_admin` | scheduling a digest that is not 32 bytes |
| 12 | `EUpgradeCapUnavailable` | `blast_admin::package_admin` | the package was made immutable |
| 13 | `ENotReady` | `delayed`; `delayed_set` for `delayed_set::apply_add`, `delayed_map` for `delayed_map::apply` | applying a proposal, or accepting a root transfer, before its `ready_at_ms` |
| 14 | `ENoPending` | the type's module | applying or cancelling when nothing is pending |
| 15 | `EInvalidDelay` | `delayed` | a notice above `delayed::max_delay_ms` (30 days), or a deadline or next notice that would overflow a Unix millisecond timestamp; choose a notice of at most 30 days |
| 16 | `EUnchanged` | the type's module | the proposal changes nothing, the member is already admitted, `remove` names an unknown member, or a map change repeats the entry's applied value (clearing an absent entry included) |
| 17 | `EProposalPending` | the type's module | destroying a delayed value, action slot, set or map while a proposal is pending; cancel it first |
| 18 | `EWrongChange` | `delayed_action` | `take_action` on a notice change, or a notice `apply_delay` on an action; checked before readiness |
| 19 | `EInvalidPauseBits` | `package_version` | pause or unpause names zero bits or a bit the package does not define |
| 20 | `EPauseUnchanged` | `package_version` | pausing only bits already set, or clearing only bits already clear |
| 21 | `EPaused` | `package_version` | the operation's pause bit is set; wait for Blast to unpause it |
| 22 | `EWrongUpgradeAction` | `blast_admin::package_admin` | the ready action is not the upgrade of this digest (authorize) or not immutability (make immutable) |
| 23 | `EUnguardedUpgradeDelay` | `blast_admin::package_admin` | clearing pause bits while the upgrade notice is zero or a pending change would make it zero |
| 24 | `EInvalidPackageWitness` | `package_version` | the package witness type given to `new_publication` is a primitive, the package's OTW, or from another package |
| 25 | `EWrongUnpauseWitness` | `package_version` | `clear_pause_bits` received a value of a type other than the package witness pinned at publication |
| 26 | `EWrongPackageWitness` | `package_version` | `blast_admin::package_admin::publisher`, `blast_admin::package_admin::publisher_mut` or `blast_admin::package_admin::make_immutable` received a value of a type other than the package witness pinned at publication |

An `OTW` that is not a genuine one-time witness aborts in the framework's
`sui::package::claim` inside `package_version::new_publication`.

The one an integrator most often meets is code 9 from `package_version`: a PTB
built against an old package ID after an upgrade.

### Pitfalls

- An `AdminWitness` exists only inside one transaction. There is no reusable
  admin token to hand to a bot; a bot needs its own `AdminCap`.
- A revoked `AdminCap` still exists in its holder's wallet. Check `ACL.admins`,
  not ownership, to know whether a cap works.
- Role names repeat across packages (`UpgradeAdmin`, `CancelAdmin`). Always
  compare the full type name, including the package address and type arguments.
- After any upgrade of a package, PTBs pinned to its old package ID abort with
  code 9.
- Only the package's own code can borrow its `Publisher`: its package witness
  is never handed out, so an integrator cannot create Display or transfer
  policies for a Blast package's types.

### Q&A

**Who can change Blast's fees or settings?** Only an `AdminCap` listed in
`ACL.admins` with the specific role, signed in within the same transaction. The
root cannot act on any package directly.

**Can Blast add a new kind of admin power later?** A new or upgraded consumer
package can declare a new role type, and root can grant it. The ACL itself is
immutable and cannot change how sign-in works.

**How do I see every Blast administrator?** Read the shared `ACL` object: each
key of `admins` is a live `AdminCap` ID and each value lists its roles. Replay
`blast_admin_events` for the full history.

**How much notice is there before root changes hands?** Seven days, fixed. The
nomination emits `delayed_action::ActionScheduled` and is visible in
`super_admin_transfer`, and root can cancel it at any time before acceptance.

**Can a role from one package authorize actions in another?** No. A consumer
function names its role type in its signature, and a role type from another
package, or the same generic role with another package's OTW, is a different
type, so the transaction does not type-check.

**How much notice is there before an upgrade?** The package's applied upgrade
notice, 48 hours from wrap. A notice change itself waits the applied notice, and
the package cannot be unpaused while any upgrade notice still to come could be zero.

**Which Blast packages can still be upgraded?** Those whose `PackageAdmin`
still holds an `UpgradeCap`. `blast_admin` and `blast_partners` are immutable.

**What stops a stale package version from moving funds?** Every protected call
checks the shared version against the version compiled into the bytecode,
and the upgrade finalizer advances the version in the same transaction that
commits the upgrade.

**What does an upgrade leave on chain?** `UpgradeAuthorized` with the exact
digest, `UpgradeCommitted` with the new package ID, and
`VersionAdvanced` with the new version, all in one transaction.

**Can someone forge a version bump event?** No. A `PackageVersion<OTW>` exists
only through `OTW`'s own publication, which needs the `OTW` value inside
its package `init`, and only `blast_admin::package_admin::commit_upgrade_and_advance`
advances it.

## API reference: `blast_presale` (Presale)

Not yet published on mainnet. Its interface may change before publication.

Events: payload structs are emitted directly, each under its own type.

Abort codes: this package aborts with the numeric codes below from whichever module detects the failure; the abort location names that module.

| Code | Constant | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | `EUnguardedDelay` | Unpausing needs every policy delay nonzero, with no pending zero delay or admission. |
| 1 | `EAllowanceUnchanged` | An allowlist update must change whether the type or partner is allowed. |
| 2 | `EQuoteNotAllowed` | This Quote type is not allowed for new presales. |
| 3 | `EVenueNotAllowed` | This venue is not allowed for new presales. |
| 4 | `EInvalidVenue` | A venue must be a non-framework struct, never a primitive, vector, or framework type any caller can construct. |
| 5 | `EInvalidFees` | Blast's raise and token shares must be at most 1,000 BPS and each LP fee at most 3,000. |
| 6 | `EInvalidAssetPair` | The sale token and Quote type must differ. |
| 7 | `EInvalidRaiseTarget` | The raise target must be positive. |
| 8 | `EInvalidTokenAllocation` | The supply must be positive, and token allocations unique, positive, bounded, totalling exactly 10,000 BPS with Blast's share, and apportioning to positive amounts. |
| 9 | `EInvalidWindow` | The commitment window must be positive, the liquidity window at least seven days, and both must end within u64 milliseconds. |
| 10 | `EInvalidEligibilityPolicy` | The eligibility policy has an invalid cap, participant bound, root, or leaf count. |
| 11 | `EInvalidLifecycle` | The presale is not in the lifecycle required by this operation. |
| 12 | `EPresaleEnded` | The presale commitment window has ended. |
| 13 | `EPresaleNotEnded` | The presale commitment window has not ended, and the sale cannot close early: its raise is not full under a hard cap that closes it when filled. |
| 14 | `EZeroCommitment` | A presale commitment must be positive. |
| 15 | `EWalletCapExceeded` | The wallet commitment exceeds its eligibility cap. |
| 16 | `EParticipantCapacityReached` | The presale already contains its maximum number of participants. |
| 17 | `EInvalidEligibilityProof` | The submitted wallet, cap, index, or proof does not match the allowlist. |
| 18 | `EWrongEligibilityPolicy` | The commit function does not match the presale eligibility policy. |
| 19 | `ETotalCommitmentOverflow` | Adding the commitment would overflow the presale total. |
| 20 | `ENoCommitment` | The wallet has no undelivered presale commitment. |
| 21 | `EWrongPresaleCap` | The creator capability belongs to a different presale. |
| 22 | `ELiquidityDeadlineNotReached` | The deadline to cancel an unlaunched funded presale has not arrived. |
| 23 | `EInitialSupplyNotZero` | The supplied SaleToken TreasuryCap must have zero total supply. |
| 24 | `EBelowMinimumCommitment` | The wallet's total commitment is below the sale's minimum commitment. |
| 25 | `EUnreachableRaise` | The minimum commitment times the slots held to it, the participant bound of an open policy or the open-to-anyone phase slots beyond any allowlist, must reach the raise target. |
| 26 | `EUnseedablePrice` | The raise and LP-token allocation give a seed price the venues cannot pool. |
| 27 | `EInvalidUncappedPhase` | An uncapped phase must start inside the window, and an open-to-anyone phase needs a positive minimum and a participant bound between the policy's and 65,536. |
| 28 | `EUncappedPhaseNotOpen` | The presale has no uncapped phase open to any wallet, or it has not started. |
| 29 | `EPresaleFilled` | The presale has already reached its raise under its hard cap. |
| 30 | `EInvalidRaiseAllocation` | Raise allocations must be unique, positive, bounded, leave the LP a share after Blast's, and apportion to positive amounts. |
| 31 | `EPresaleNotStarted` | The presale commitment window has not started. |
| 32 | `EPresaleStarted` | A presale's Blast rates can change only before its commitment window starts. |
| 33 | `EProtocolFeesUnchanged` | A presale fee update must change its stored rates. |
| 34 | `EInvalidHardCap` | A hard cap must start inside the commitment window. |
| 35 | `EMissingSetting` | A presale needs its eligibility policy and LP-fee split set before it is finalized. |
| 36 | `ESaleTokenNotUnregulated` | The sale currency must be confirmed unregulated; regulated and unknown legacy currencies are not allowed. |
| 37 | `EAboveFeePolicy` | A sale fee override cannot exceed the currently applied fee policy. |
| 38 | `EProtocolFeesIncreased` | A shared sale's fee override may only keep or lower each of its rates. |

### `blast_presale::blast_presale`

Standalone presales with capped commitments, proportional fills or a first-come hard cap, migration-gated claims, full refunds when a sale does not migrate, the migration hand-off to the sale's venue, and the owner proof its vault accepts.

Source: https://github.com/interest-protocol/blast-v2-contracts/blob/main/sui/presale/sources/blast_presale.move

#### Types

```move
/// Shared singleton every presale's object ID derives from, so a client finds a coin's one sale
/// from the coin type alone.
public struct PresaleRegistry has key {
    id: UID,
}

/// Derives the one presale of `SaleToken` from the registry.
public struct PresaleKey<phantom SaleToken>() has copy, drop, store;

/// Who may commit and the maximum Quote each wallet may commit.
///
/// `Open` gives every wallet the same cap and minimum. The minimum times the
/// participant bound must reach the raise, so filling every slot funds the sale
/// and dust commitments cannot lock real buyers out. `Allowlisted` commits one
/// cap per wallet in a positional Blake2b-256 Merkle tree, supporting equal,
/// tiered, or fully custom caps.
public enum EligibilityPolicy has copy, drop, store {
    Open {
        wallet_cap: u64,
        max_participants: u64,
        min_commitment: u64,
    },
    Allowlisted {
        root: vector<u8>,
        leaf_count: u64,
    },
}

/// Who may commit once an uncapped phase lifts wallet caps.
public enum UncappedAccess has copy, drop, store {
    /// Only wallets the sale's eligibility policy admits, without their caps.
    Eligible,
    /// Any wallet, bounded like an open policy: `min_commitment` over the slots held to it must
    /// reach the raise so dust cannot lock buyers out. Every slot counts under an open policy;
    /// under an allowlist only the slots beyond its leaves do, since allowlisted wallets may
    /// commit any positive amount.
    Anyone {
        max_participants: u64,
        min_commitment: u64,
    },
}

/// An optional closing phase, starting `starts_after_ms` into the commitment window,
/// that lifts wallet caps. Whether the sale then overflows or stops at its raise is the
/// sale's `HardCap`, not the phase's.
public struct UncappedPhase has copy, drop, store {
    starts_after_ms: u64,
    access: UncappedAccess,
}

/// From `starts_after_ms` into the commitment window, the sale takes Quote only up to its
/// raise, first come, first served: a commitment takes what is left and returns the excess at
/// once, and the sale stops accepting Quote when the raise is full. Before then it overflows,
/// filling every wallet at one common rate. With `closes_when_filled`, a sale whose raise is full
/// under its hard cap may settle at once instead of waiting for the window's end.
public struct HardCap has copy, drop, store {
    starts_after_ms: u64,
    closes_when_filled: bool,
}

/// The presale's one-way lifecycle.
public enum Lifecycle has copy, drop, store {
    Pending,
    Open,
    Funded,
    Migrated,
    Cancelled,
}

/// One creator's authority over one presale.
public struct PresaleCap has key, store {
    id: UID,
    presale_id: ID,
}

/// One recipient's share, in BPS, of the token supply or of the raise, paid at migration or
/// vested from it as its `blast_core::payout::Recipient` says.
public struct RecipientShare has copy, drop, store {
    recipient: blast_core::payout::Recipient,
    bps: blast_core::bps::Bps,
}

/// The exact token or Quote amount one recipient receives at migration, apportioned from its
/// `RecipientShare` when the presale is created.
public struct RecipientPayout has copy, drop, store {
    recipient: blast_core::payout::Recipient,
    amount: u64,
}

/// Dynamic-field name for one wallet's undelivered commitment.
public struct CommitmentKey(address) has copy, drop, store;

/// One wallet's Quote commitment and immutable cap.
public struct Commitment has copy, drop, store {
    quote: u64,
    wallet_cap: u64,
}

/// Hot potato from `new` to `finalize`, collecting the creator's settings. Only `finalize`
/// consumes it, so every sale is finalized in the transaction whose `new` checked the creation
/// policy and snapshotted Blast's rates. `finalize` validates the settings together; the supply,
/// token allocations, raise, windows, eligibility policy, and the vault's LP-fee split must all be
/// set.
public struct PresaleInitializer<phantom SaleToken, phantom Quote> {
    treasury_cap: TreasuryCap<SaleToken>,
    venue: TypeName,
    protocol_fees: fee_policy::ProtocolFees,
    token_supply: u64,
    burnable: bool,
    token_allocation_bps: blast_core::bps::Bps,
    liquidity_token_allocation_bps: blast_core::bps::Bps,
    recipient_allocations: vector<RecipientShare>,
    participant_vesting: Option<blast_core::payout::VestingTerms>,
    raise_target: u64,
    raise_allocations: vector<RecipientShare>,
    duration_ms: u64,
    liquidity_window_ms: u64,
    eligibility: Option<EligibilityPolicy>,
    uncapped: Option<UncappedPhase>,
    hard_cap: Option<HardCap>,
    fee_split: Option<blast_core::fee_split::FeeSplit>,
    partner_id: Option<ID>,
}

/// One standalone presale and its complete custody until migration or refund.
///
/// The complete fixed or burn-only token supply is apportioned at creation.
/// Presale, LP, Blast, and additional recipient allocations stay escrowed until
/// a funded migration atomically releases them. Blast's rates are snapshotted
/// at creation, Blast's `FeeAdmin` may change them until the window starts, and its
/// fees move into the sale's protocol-fee ledger on migration, which pays them to the treasury at
/// once, or, when the sale names a Blast partner, holds them until
/// `pay_protocol_fees_with_partner` pays the partner its cut of each and the treasury the rest.
/// If the raise is missed, every commitment
/// is refunded. Anyone may migrate a funded sale until it is cancelled; once LP
/// is still unmigrated at its deadline, anyone may cancel it so every
/// commitment becomes refundable. Under participant vesting, each claim locks the
/// participant's tokens in its own schedule instead of paying them out.
public struct Presale<phantom SaleToken, phantom Quote> has key {
    id: UID,
    presale_cap_id: ID,
    lifecycle: Lifecycle,
    /// The commitment window's length: as created until the sale closes early, then the time it
    /// ran.
    duration_ms: u64,
    liquidity_window_ms: u64,
    /// When commitments open, fixed by `share`; zero until then. The window's end, the LP
    /// deadline, and the uncapped and hard-cap starts are derived from it and the lengths above.
    start_ms: u64,
    raise_target: u64,
    eligibility: EligibilityPolicy,
    uncapped: Option<UncappedPhase>,
    hard_cap: Option<HardCap>,
    /// The venue witness type the sale's liquidity migrates to; only it redeems the hand-off.
    venue: TypeName,
    /// The LP-fee split the sale's vault starts with.
    fee_split: blast_core::fee_split::FeeSplit,
    total_commitments: u64,
    /// The wallets holding an undelivered commitment: admitted by their first commitment and
    /// released by their claim, so the claim that empties the sale is the last one.
    participants: u64,
    quote: Balance<Quote>,
    token_allocation: u64,
    participant_vesting: Option<blast_core::payout::VestingTerms>,
    sale_tokens: Balance<SaleToken>,
    liquidity_tokens: Balance<SaleToken>,
    recipient_payouts: vector<RecipientPayout>,
    recipient_tokens: Balance<SaleToken>,
    raise_payouts: vector<RecipientPayout>,
    protocol_fees: fee_policy::ProtocolFees,
    protocol_quote: u64,
    protocol_tokens: Balance<SaleToken>,
    /// The Blast partner named at creation, paid its cut of Blast's fees. It never changes once
    /// the sale is shared.
    partner_id: Option<ID>,
    /// Blast's raise and token fees from migration until paid; bound to `partner_id`.
    fee_ledger: blast_core::protocol_fees::Ledger<SaleToken, Quote>,
}
```

#### Functions

```move
/// Creates one equal-cap policy with a bounded number of distinct wallets, each
/// of which must commit at least `min_commitment` in total.
public fun open_eligibility(
    wallet_cap: u64,
    max_participants: u64,
    min_commitment: u64,
): EligibilityPolicy

/// Creates one allowlist policy whose leaves are `(index, wallet, wallet_cap)`.
public fun allowlisted_eligibility(root: vector<u8>, leaf_count: u64): EligibilityPolicy

/// Lifts wallet caps for eligible wallets `start_delay_ms` into the window.
public fun uncapped_for_eligible(start_delay_ms: u64): UncappedPhase

/// Opens the sale to any wallet without caps `start_delay_ms` into the window, admitting
/// at most `max_participants` wallets in total, each committing at least `min_commitment`.
public fun uncapped_for_anyone(
    start_delay_ms: u64,
    max_participants: u64,
    min_commitment: u64,
): UncappedPhase

/// One recipient's share in BPS of the supply or the raise, paid or vested at migration as
/// `recipient` says. Presale creation validates each list of shares under that list's own rules
/// and error.
public fun recipient_share(
    recipient: blast_core::payout::Recipient,
    bps: blast_core::bps::Bps,
): RecipientShare

/// Starts a presale of `SaleToken` raising `Quote` whose liquidity migrates to the venue that
/// issued `venue_ticket` for the pair, and snapshots Blast's rates. The venue keeps the pool terms,
/// such as a CLMM tier, which it records while preparing the ticket.
///
/// A venue in this or any other package issues tickets sealed by its own witness, which only its
/// defining module can construct. The `CreationPolicy` must admit that venue, so Blast decides
/// which venues may open sales; the sale's migration hand-off is then redeemable only by it.
public fun new<SaleToken, Quote>(
    treasury_cap: TreasuryCap<SaleToken>,
    package_version: &blast_admin::package_version::PackageVersion<blast_presale_package::BLAST_PRESALE_PACKAGE>,
    venue_ticket: blast_core::migration::VenueTicket<SaleToken, Quote>,
    creation_policy: &creation_policy::CreationPolicy,
    fee_policy: &fee_policy::FeePolicy,
): PresaleInitializer<SaleToken, Quote>

/// Sets the complete supply `finalize` mints, and whether it then becomes burn-only rather than
/// fixed.
public fun set_supply<SaleToken, Quote>(
    self: &mut PresaleInitializer<SaleToken, Quote>,
    package_version: &blast_admin::package_version::PackageVersion<blast_presale_package::BLAST_PRESALE_PACKAGE>,
    token_supply: u64,
    burnable: bool,
)

/// Splits the supply in BPS between the buyers, the LP, and each recipient. With Blast's token
/// rate the shares must total exactly 10,000 BPS.
public fun set_token_allocations<SaleToken, Quote>(
    self: &mut PresaleInitializer<SaleToken, Quote>,
    package_version: &blast_admin::package_version::PackageVersion<blast_presale_package::BLAST_PRESALE_PACKAGE>,
    token_allocation_bps: blast_core::bps::Bps,
    liquidity_token_allocation_bps: blast_core::bps::Bps,
    recipient_allocations: vector<RecipientShare>,
)

/// Locks each participant's claimed tokens in its own schedule under `vesting_terms`, starting at
/// its claim, instead of paying them out. Without it, claims pay tokens out at once.
```
