## API reference: `blast_migrators` (Cetus and Bluefin venues)

Not yet published on mainnet. Its interface may change before publication.

Events: payload structs are emitted directly, each under its own type.

Abort codes: this package aborts with the numeric codes below from whichever module detects the failure; the abort location names that module.

| Code | Constant | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | `EInvalidCoinOrder` | `CoinA` and `CoinB` must follow the Cetus coin order. |
| 1 | `EPositionPoolMismatch` | The pool must be the vault's own pool. |
| 2 | `EWrongCoinPair` | `CoinA` and `CoinB` must be exactly the sale's Meme and Quote. |
| 3 | `EInvalidTier` | A Bluefin tier needs a tick spacing in 1..=400 and a fee rate in 1..=20,000. |
| 4 | `ESymbolTooLong` | A Bluefin Meme symbol must be at most 32 bytes. |

### `blast_migrators::blast_migrators`

The migrators package's publication.  `init` turns the one-time witness into `blast_admin`'s owned `Publication`, which the publisher wraps with the package's `UpgradeCap` through `blast_admin::package_admin::wrap`; that shares `PackageVersion<BLAST_MIGRATORS>` and `PackageAdmin<BLAST_MIGRATORS>`. Venues define no pause bits, so the version starts unpaused and the package has no unpause. Residual risk: the package has no emergency stop of its own. Migration stops with each product's migration pause bit and `buyback_and_burn` with the vault's admin bit, but `prepare`, `collect_fees`, and `settle_and_apply_fee_split` can be stopped only by advancing this package's version through a delayed upgrade, which retires every call to the old bytecode. Upgrades are scheduled, authorized and committed through the generic `package_admin` under this package's own `UpgradeAdmin<BLAST_MIGRATORS>` role. The products never import this package: each venue redeems the `Migration` its product's own `migrate` returned earlier in the transaction.

Source: https://github.com/interest-protocol/blast-v2-contracts/blob/main/sui/migrators/sources/blast_migrators.move

#### Types

```move
/// The package's one-time witness (OTW), typing its version, administration, and roles.
public struct BLAST_MIGRATORS() has drop;

/// The package witness `blast_admin` pins at publication, the one type that authorizes this
/// package's own administration calls such as unpause. Only this module could construct it, and it
/// is never stored or returned; the package defines no pause bits, so nothing constructs it.
public struct PackageWitness() has drop;
```

### `blast_migrators::bluefin`

Bluefin coin preparation, migration into `blast_vault` custody, fee collection with auto-LP, settled fee-split updates, and buybacks over custodied concentrated-liquidity principal, for launches and presales alike.  Bluefin pools are keyed by their exact type-parameter order, so this module always creates and expects `Pool<Meme, Quote>` with Meme as coin A.

Source: https://github.com/interest-protocol/blast-v2-contracts/blob/main/sui/migrators/sources/venues/bluefin.move

#### Types

```move
/// The Bluefin venue's sealed witness: it issues tickets, redeems migrations, and keys the position
/// in the vault, so each product's venue list and the vault registry admit this one type.
public struct Venue() has drop;

/// A prepared coin's Bluefin pool tier.
public struct PoolTier has copy, drop, store {
    tick_spacing: u32,
    fee_rate: u64,
}

/// Sealed `VenueConfig` field name for the Meme type's Bluefin pool tier.
public struct PoolTierKey<phantom Meme>() has copy, drop, store;
```

#### Functions

```move
/// Prepares `Meme` for a Bluefin sale in `Quote` at the creator's tier, recording the tier, and
/// returns the ticket the product's `new` redeems. `treasury_cap` proves the caller controls the
/// coin, so no one else can record its tier first.
///
/// Bluefin checks the tier only when migration creates the pool, and a sale cannot change its
/// tier, so the same bounds apply here first. The pool and its position store the Meme symbol, so
/// it is bounded here too.
public fun prepare<Meme, Quote>(
    migrators_version: &blast_admin::package_version::PackageVersion<blast_migrators::BLAST_MIGRATORS>,
    venue_config: &mut venue_config::VenueConfig,
    _: &TreasuryCap<Meme>,
    currency: &Currency<Meme>,
    tick_spacing: u32,
    fee_rate: u64,
): blast_core::migration::VenueTicket<Meme, Quote>

/// Migrates a sale into a new full-range pool at the recorded tier and a `blast_vault` vault:
/// `migration` is the hand-off the launch's or presale's own `migrate` returned earlier in the
/// transaction.
///
/// Redeems the hand-off. The opening price derives from the handed-off balances, which
/// seed the position on the side `is_meme_seed_side` chooses. `creation_fee` is paid whole, and
/// Bluefin aborts unless it is exactly the configured SUI fee. The position and the venue
/// residuals go to the vault, which has no withdrawal path. The caller receives no object; Bluefin
/// records it as the new pool's manager, a role limited to the pool's reward emissions and to
/// handing the role on (ADR 0088).
public fun migrate<Meme, Quote>(
    migration: blast_core::migration::Migration<Meme, Quote>,
    migrators_version: &blast_admin::package_version::PackageVersion<blast_migrators::BLAST_MIGRATORS>,
    venue_config: &venue_config::VenueConfig,
    currency: &Currency<Meme>,
    quote_currency: &Currency<Quote>,
    bluefin_config: &mut config::GlobalConfig,
    registry: &mut blast_vault::blast_vault_package::VaultRegistry,
    vault_version: &blast_admin::package_version::PackageVersion<blast_vault::blast_vault_package::BLAST_VAULT_PACKAGE>,
    treasury: &blast_core::blast_treasury::Treasury,
    creation_fee: Coin<sui::SUI>,
    clock: &Clock,
    ctx: &mut TxContext,
)

/// Collects the custodied position's fees, splits them, burns the burn share's Meme, and adds the
/// auto-LP share back to the position. Anyone may call it.
public fun collect_fees<Meme, Quote>(
    self: &mut blast_vault::vault::Vault<Meme, Quote>,
    migrators_version: &blast_admin::package_version::PackageVersion<blast_migrators::BLAST_MIGRATORS>,
    vault_version: &blast_admin::package_version::PackageVersion<blast_vault::blast_vault_package::BLAST_VAULT_PACKAGE>,
    treasury: &blast_core::blast_treasury::Treasury,
    currency: &mut Currency<Meme>,
    bluefin_config: &config::GlobalConfig,
    pool: &mut pool::Pool<Meme, Quote>,
    clock: &Clock,
    ctx: &mut TxContext,
)

/// Anyone may settle accrued fees under the current split, then apply the stored ready proposal.
public fun settle_and_apply_fee_split<Meme, Quote>(
    self: &mut blast_vault::vault::Vault<Meme, Quote>,
    migrators_version: &blast_admin::package_version::PackageVersion<blast_migrators::BLAST_MIGRATORS>,
    vault_version: &blast_admin::package_version::PackageVersion<blast_vault::blast_vault_package::BLAST_VAULT_PACKAGE>,
    treasury: &blast_core::blast_treasury::Treasury,
    currency: &mut Currency<Meme>,
    bluefin_config: &config::GlobalConfig,
    pool: &mut pool::Pool<Meme, Quote>,
    clock: &Clock,
    ctx: &mut TxContext,
)

/// Adds the vault's waiting auto-LP Meme and Quote to its position in `pool` at the current price
/// and keeps the rest for the next call. Anyone may call it, apart from collection, so a Bluefin
/// refusal of the add never blocks collecting fees.
public fun compound_auto_lp<Meme, Quote>(
    self: &mut blast_vault::vault::Vault<Meme, Quote>,
    migrators_version: &blast_admin::package_version::PackageVersion<blast_migrators::BLAST_MIGRATORS>,
    vault_version: &blast_admin::package_version::PackageVersion<blast_vault::blast_vault_package::BLAST_VAULT_PACKAGE>,
    bluefin_config: &config::GlobalConfig,
    pool: &mut pool::Pool<Meme, Quote>,
    clock: &Clock,
)

/// Swaps `quote_in` of the vault's burn Quote for Meme in its pool and burns it, under a buyback
/// admin. Aborts unless `quote_in` is positive and at most the burn Quote held, and unless the swap
/// returns at least `min_meme_out`; the admin sets it from an off-chain price, since anyone can move
/// the pool's price within a transaction. Quote the pool does not take stays for the next buyback.
public fun buyback_and_burn<Meme, Quote>(
    self: &mut blast_vault::vault::Vault<Meme, Quote>,
    migrators_version: &blast_admin::package_version::PackageVersion<blast_migrators::BLAST_MIGRATORS>,
    vault_version: &blast_admin::package_version::PackageVersion<blast_vault::blast_vault_package::BLAST_VAULT_PACKAGE>,
    admin_witness: &blast_admin::blast_acl::AdminWitness<blast_core::blast_domain::BuybackAdmin>,
    currency: &mut Currency<Meme>,
    bluefin_config: &config::GlobalConfig,
    pool: &mut pool::Pool<Meme, Quote>,
    quote_in: u64,
    min_meme_out: u64,
    clock: &Clock,
    ctx: &mut TxContext,
)
```

### `blast_migrators::cetus`

Cetus coin preparation, pool-creation reservation, migration into `blast_vault` custody, and collection, for launches and presales alike.  Anyone holding Meme can create a Cetus pool, and Cetus allows one pool per pair and tick spacing, so a buyer could pre-create the migration pool at a price of their choosing. Preparing the coin therefore mints the Meme type's single Cetus `PoolCreationCap` from its treasury capability, before any Meme can leave the sale's custody, registers the pair at the creator's tick spacing, and returns a `VenueTicket` for that pair the sale redeems; afterwards only that capability or Cetus's pool-manager role can create the pair's pool there. Trusting that role is a venue-operator assumption: a pool it creates first makes the pair's migration abort, and only a migrators upgrade could recover the sale. The capability stays in `VenueConfig` under a key only this module constructs, with no extraction or unregistration path.  Migration redeems the `Migration` the sale's own `migrate` returned earlier in the transaction and burns the full-range position through Cetus LP Burn, so Cetus itself records the sale's liquidity as permanently locked; the `blast_vault` vault keeps the `CetusLPBurnProof`, which can only collect fees. A burned position cannot receive liquidity, so auto-LP adds to a second full-range position the vault opens on first use and keeps with no removal path.  Cetus orders a pool's coin types by type name. Each route after `prepare` takes the pool's coin types as `CoinA` and `CoinB` beside the sale's `Meme` and `Quote`, proves they are the same pair, and retypes balances between the two orders through a checked dynamic-field round trip (ADR 0100).

Source: https://github.com/interest-protocol/blast-v2-contracts/blob/main/sui/migrators/sources/venues/cetus.move

#### Types

```move
/// The Cetus venue's sealed witness: it issues tickets, redeems migrations, and keys the position
/// in the vault, so each product's venue list and the vault registry admit this one type.
public struct Venue() has drop;

/// Sealed `VenueConfig` object-field name for the Meme type's Cetus `PoolCreationCap`.
///
/// The capability is a dynamic object field, so it keeps the ID that Cetus's permission registry
/// and every `CetusPoolReserved` event record, and stays readable by that ID.
public struct CreationCapKey<phantom Meme>() has copy, drop, store;

/// Sealed `VenueConfig` field name for the Meme type's Cetus tick spacing.
public struct PoolTierKey<phantom Meme>() has copy, drop, store;

/// Transient dynamic-field name `cast` uses to retype a coin or balance.
public struct CastKey() has copy, drop, store;
```

#### Functions

```move
/// Prepares `Meme` for a Cetus sale in `Quote` at the creator's `tick_spacing`, reserving Cetus
/// pool creation for the pair, and returns the ticket the product's `new` redeems.
///
/// The Meme type's single `PoolCreationCap` is minted from `treasury_cap` before any Meme can
/// leave the sale's custody, the pair is registered at `tick_spacing`, and the spacing is recorded.
/// Aborts, leaving Cetus unchanged, when Cetus does not register the spacing or refuses the pair
/// at it, so the creator can choose another tier or venue instead.
public fun prepare<Meme, Quote>(
    migrators_version: &blast_admin::package_version::PackageVersion<blast_migrators::BLAST_MIGRATORS>,
    venue_config: &mut venue_config::VenueConfig,
    cetus_config: &config::GlobalConfig,
    pools: &mut factory::Pools,
    treasury_cap: &mut TreasuryCap<Meme>,
    tick_spacing: u32,
    ctx: &mut TxContext,
): blast_core::migration::VenueTicket<Meme, Quote>

/// Migrates a sale into a Cetus pool and a `blast_vault` vault: `migration` is the hand-off the
/// launch's or presale's own `migrate` returned earlier in the transaction. `CoinA` and `CoinB`
/// name the sale's Meme and Quote in Cetus's canonical coin order.
///
/// Redeems the hand-off, creates the pair's pool with the reserved capability at the recorded
/// tick spacing, priced from the handed-off balances, seeds full-range liquidity with exactly
/// those balances on the side `is_coin_a_seed_side` chooses, burns the position, and creates the
/// vault from the sale's terms with the burn proof and Cetus's residual. Any Cetus refusal,
/// including a tier Cetus no longer registers, aborts the whole transaction, the product's
/// `migrate` with it, so the sale stays ready to migrate.
public fun migrate<Meme, Quote, CoinA, CoinB>(
    migration: blast_core::migration::Migration<Meme, Quote>,
    migrators_version: &blast_admin::package_version::PackageVersion<blast_migrators::BLAST_MIGRATORS>,
    venue_config: &venue_config::VenueConfig,
    cetus_config: &config::GlobalConfig,
    pools: &mut factory::Pools,
    burn_manager: &mut lp_burn::BurnManager,
    registry: &mut blast_vault::blast_vault_package::VaultRegistry,
    vault_version: &blast_admin::package_version::PackageVersion<blast_vault::blast_vault_package::BLAST_VAULT_PACKAGE>,
    treasury: &blast_core::blast_treasury::Treasury,
    clock: &Clock,
    ctx: &mut TxContext,
)

/// Collects the vault position's fees from its pool, splits them, and burns the burn share's Meme;
/// the auto-LP share waits in the vault for `compound_auto_lp`. Anyone may call it. `CoinA` and
/// `CoinB` are the pool's coin order.
public fun collect_fees<Meme, Quote, CoinA, CoinB>(
    self: &mut blast_vault::vault::Vault<Meme, Quote>,
    migrators_version: &blast_admin::package_version::PackageVersion<blast_migrators::BLAST_MIGRATORS>,
    vault_version: &blast_admin::package_version::PackageVersion<blast_vault::blast_vault_package::BLAST_VAULT_PACKAGE>,
    treasury: &blast_core::blast_treasury::Treasury,
    currency: &mut Currency<Meme>,
    cetus_config: &config::GlobalConfig,
    burn_manager: &lp_burn::BurnManager,
    pool: &mut pool::Pool<CoinA, CoinB>,
    ctx: &mut TxContext,
)

/// Anyone may settle accrued fees under the current split, then apply the stored ready proposal. `CoinA`
/// and `CoinB` are the pool's coin order.
public fun settle_and_apply_fee_split<Meme, Quote, CoinA, CoinB>(
    self: &mut blast_vault::vault::Vault<Meme, Quote>,
    migrators_version: &blast_admin::package_version::PackageVersion<blast_migrators::BLAST_MIGRATORS>,
    vault_version: &blast_admin::package_version::PackageVersion<blast_vault::blast_vault_package::BLAST_VAULT_PACKAGE>,
    treasury: &blast_core::blast_treasury::Treasury,
    currency: &mut Currency<Meme>,
    cetus_config: &config::GlobalConfig,
    burn_manager: &lp_burn::BurnManager,
    pool: &mut pool::Pool<CoinA, CoinB>,
    clock: &Clock,
    ctx: &mut TxContext,
)

/// Adds the vault's waiting auto-LP Meme and Quote to its auto-LP position in `pool` at the
/// current price and keeps the rest for the next call. Anyone may call it, apart from collection,
/// so a Cetus refusal of the add never blocks collecting fees. `CoinA` and `CoinB` are the pool's
/// coin order.
public fun compound_auto_lp<Meme, Quote, CoinA, CoinB>(
    self: &mut blast_vault::vault::Vault<Meme, Quote>,
    migrators_version: &blast_admin::package_version::PackageVersion<blast_migrators::BLAST_MIGRATORS>,
    vault_version: &blast_admin::package_version::PackageVersion<blast_vault::blast_vault_package::BLAST_VAULT_PACKAGE>,
    cetus_config: &config::GlobalConfig,
    pool: &mut pool::Pool<CoinA, CoinB>,
    clock: &Clock,
    ctx: &mut TxContext,
)

/// Swaps `quote_in` of the vault's burn Quote for Meme in its pool and burns it, under a buyback
/// admin. Aborts unless `quote_in` is positive and at most the burn Quote held, and unless the swap
/// returns at least `min_meme_out`; the admin sets it from an off-chain price, since anyone can move
/// the pool's price within a transaction. Quote the pool does not take stays for the next buyback.
/// `CoinA` and `CoinB` are the pool's coin order.
public fun buyback_and_burn<Meme, Quote, CoinA, CoinB>(
    self: &mut blast_vault::vault::Vault<Meme, Quote>,
    migrators_version: &blast_admin::package_version::PackageVersion<blast_migrators::BLAST_MIGRATORS>,
    vault_version: &blast_admin::package_version::PackageVersion<blast_vault::blast_vault_package::BLAST_VAULT_PACKAGE>,
    admin_witness: &blast_admin::blast_acl::AdminWitness<blast_core::blast_domain::BuybackAdmin>,
    currency: &mut Currency<Meme>,
    cetus_config: &config::GlobalConfig,
    pool: &mut pool::Pool<CoinA, CoinB>,
    quote_in: u64,
    min_meme_out: u64,
    clock: &Clock,
    ctx: &mut TxContext,
)
```

### `blast_migrators::constants`

Package-wide migrator constants exposed as zero-cost macros.

Source: https://github.com/interest-protocol/blast-v2-contracts/blob/main/sui/migrators/sources/lib/constants.move

#### Constants

- `version: u64 = 1`: The package version this bytecode serves.
- `bluefin_max_tick_spacing: u32 = 400`: Bluefin pool creation's own tick-spacing bound (`pool` aborts 1026 above it).
- `bluefin_max_fee_rate: u64 = 20_000`: Bluefin pool creation's own fee-rate bound (`pool` aborts 1027 above it).
- `max_meme_symbol_length: u64 = 32`: Longest Meme symbol, in bytes, a Bluefin pool accepts: the pool and its position store the symbol, and the pool name repeats it, so a longer one would make the position too large.
- `min_swap_sqrt_price: u128 = 4_295_048_017`: Lowest sqrt price a Cetus or Bluefin swap accepts as its limit; buybacks selling Quote as coin A run to it and rely on the caller's minimum Meme out instead.
- `max_swap_sqrt_price: u128 = 79_226_673_515_401_279_992_447_579_054`: Highest sqrt price a Cetus or Bluefin swap accepts as its limit, for buybacks selling Quote as coin B.
- `q64_shift: u8 = 64`: Fractional bits of a Q64.64 sqrt price.
- `q128_shift: u8 = 128`: Fractional bits of a Q128 value; a fixed-A auto-LP liquidity must stay below it.
- `auto_lp_margin: u256 = 2`: Atoms of the other asset kept in reserve beyond the estimate, covering the venue's own rounding of the liquidity it derives from the fixed amount.

### `blast_migrators::events`

Event payloads and their package-only emitters for `blast_migrators`: the pool tier each venue records while preparing a pair. Vault creation, LP-fee collection, auto-LP, buybacks, and holder rewards emit from `blast_vault`; versions and upgrades from `blast_admin`.

Source: https://github.com/interest-protocol/blast-v2-contracts/blob/main/sui/migrators/sources/lib/events.move

#### Events

```move
/// Cetus pool creation for the pair is reserved under `pool_creation_cap_id`, the Meme type's one
/// `PoolCreationCap`, at the tick spacing its migration uses.
public struct CetusPoolReserved<phantom Meme, phantom Quote> has copy, drop {
    pool_creation_cap_id: ID,
    tick_spacing: u32,
}

/// The Bluefin pool tier the pair's migration uses.
public struct BluefinPoolTierRecorded<phantom Meme, phantom Quote> has copy, drop {
    tick_spacing: u32,
    fee_rate: u64,
}
```

### `blast_migrators::venue_config`

Shared venue state: write-once entries only their venue module can key.  Venue modules add authority-bearing objects (the Meme type's Cetus `PoolCreationCap`) as dynamic object fields, so each object keeps its ID and stays readable by it, and plain records (a prepared coin's pool tier) as dynamic fields, while preparing a coin. No entry is ever removed, replaced, or borrowed mutably. New venue modules add entries without changing this object's layout.

Source: https://github.com/interest-protocol/blast-v2-contracts/blob/main/sui/migrators/sources/venues/venue_config.move

#### Types

```move
/// Shared singleton holding venue-owned entries.
public struct VenueConfig has key {
    id: UID,
}
```

## API reference: `blast_partners` (Partner codes)

Not yet published on mainnet. Its interface may change before publication.

Events: payload structs are emitted directly, each under its own type.

Abort codes: this package aborts with the numeric codes below from whichever module detects the failure; the abort location names that module.

| Code | Constant | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | `EInvalidRecipient` | A partner's recipient must not be the zero address. |
| 1 | `EShareAboveMax` | A partner's share must be at most 80% of Blast's fee. |
| 2 | `EUnchanged` | An update must change the value it sets or proposes. |
| 3 | `ENotLiveCap` | Only the partner's applied cap may set its recipient. |
| 4 | `EPartnerNotAccepted` | The partner list does not accept the partner now. |

### `blast_partners::blast_partners`

Blast partner codes, shared by every Blast product.  A partner is one deal: it is paid a share of the fee Blast charges on every trade that names it, in the same transaction. A company holds one `PartnerCap` for all its deals, each a separate partner with its own share. Blast's partner administrator registers partners under a cap, proposes each one's share, and can propose moving a partner to another cap; the cap's holder sets where each of its partners is paid. Initial terms apply at registration. A later share or cap applies only when someone applies it, no sooner than `PARTNER_CHANGE_DELAY_MS` after it was proposed. That delay is fixed: this module never changes it, and the package is published immutable. The recipient the cap holder sets applies at once.  Products call `pay` with Blast's own fee on a trade. `pay` emits `PartnerPaid` for what the partner received; the product records the trade and the amount in its own event. Share and cap lifecycle events come from `blast_admin::delayed`, keyed by `ShareKey` and `CapKey` and owned by the partner.

Source: https://github.com/interest-protocol/blast-v2-contracts/blob/main/sui/partners/sources/blast_partners.move

#### Types

```move
/// The one administrator role in the shared Blast ACL: register partners, and
/// propose or cancel shares and moves between caps.
public struct PartnerAdmin {}

/// One Blast partner. Shared, and read by immutable reference on every trade that names it. It has
/// no destroy: launches, presales, and vaults bind its ID for good and pay Blast's held fees only
/// with it, so deleting it would strand those fees. A zero share switches it off instead.
public struct Partner has key {
    id: UID,
    /// Where the partner's share is sent; set by the live cap's holder.
    recipient: address,
    /// The partner's share of Blast's fee on each trade, in basis points.
    share_bps: blast_admin::delayed::Delayed<ShareKey, u64>,
    /// The only cap that may set `recipient`; one cap may manage many partners.
    cap_id: blast_admin::delayed::Delayed<CapKey, ID>,
}

/// Keys a partner share's delayed lifecycle.
public struct ShareKey() has copy, drop, store;

/// Keys a partner managing cap's delayed lifecycle.
public struct CapKey() has copy, drop, store;

/// A company's authority over the recipient of every partner bound to it.
public struct PartnerCap has key, store {
    id: UID,
}
```

#### Functions

```move
/// Mints a cap. It controls nothing until Blast registers a partner under it,
/// so anyone may mint one, a company included.
public fun new_cap(ctx: &mut TxContext): PartnerCap

/// Registers and shares a partner managed by the cap `cap_id`, with its share
/// and managing cap in force immediately.
public fun register(
    _: &blast_admin::blast_acl::AdminWitness<PartnerAdmin>,
    cap_id: ID,
    recipient: address,
    share_bps: u64,
    ctx: &mut TxContext,
)

/// Proposes `share_bps` as the partner's share, applicable by anyone after the fixed
/// delay. A different proposal replaces a pending one and restarts the full delay;
/// `cancel_share` discards one, even after its delay has elapsed. Proposing the
/// applied or the pending share aborts.
public fun schedule_share(
    self: &mut Partner,
    _: &blast_admin::blast_acl::AdminWitness<PartnerAdmin>,
    share_bps: u64,
    clock: &Clock,
)

/// Applies the proposed share once its delay has elapsed. Anyone may call, the partner included.
public fun apply_share(self: &mut Partner, clock: &Clock)

/// Discards the proposed share, even a ready one, keeping the applied share.
public fun cancel_share(self: &mut Partner, _: &blast_admin::blast_acl::AdminWitness<PartnerAdmin>)

/// Proposes the cap `cap_id` to manage the partner, to replace a lost or stolen
/// cap, applicable by anyone after the fixed delay. The applied cap keeps working
/// until then. A different proposal replaces a pending one and restarts the full
/// delay; `cancel_cap` discards one, even after its delay has elapsed. Proposing
/// the applied or the pending cap aborts.
public fun schedule_cap(
    self: &mut Partner,
    _: &blast_admin::blast_acl::AdminWitness<PartnerAdmin>,
    cap_id: ID,
    clock: &Clock,
)

/// Applies the proposed managing cap once its delay has elapsed. Anyone may call.
public fun apply_cap(self: &mut Partner, clock: &Clock)

/// Discards the proposed managing cap, even a ready one, keeping the applied cap.
public fun cancel_cap(self: &mut Partner, _: &blast_admin::blast_acl::AdminWitness<PartnerAdmin>)

/// Sets where the partner is paid, at once. Only the applied cap may.
public fun set_recipient(self: &mut Partner, cap: &PartnerCap, recipient: address)

/// Destroys a cap, live or not.
public fun destroy_cap(cap: PartnerCap)

/// Transfers the partner its applied share of `fee` (Blast's fee on one trade) as a
/// coin, rounded down so Blast keeps the remainder, emits `PartnerPaid`, and returns
/// the amount sent. Nothing is sent or emitted while the share is zero. `fee`
/// keeps the rest. Anyone calling it pays the partner from their own balance.
public fun pay<T>(self: &Partner, fee: &mut Balance<T>, ctx: &mut TxContext): u64

/// The fixed delay every change Blast makes to a partner waits. Products use it
/// for their own delay, such as how long a partner they remove stays accepted.
public fun delay_ms(): u64

/// The largest share of Blast's fee one partner may earn, in basis points: 8,000.
public fun max_share_bps(): u64

/// Where the partner's share is sent now.
public fun recipient(self: &Partner): address

/// The applied share of Blast's fee, in basis points; `pay` uses it.
public fun share_bps(self: &Partner): u64

/// The proposed share with its ready time, if any. It changes nothing until applied.
public fun pending_share_bps(self: &Partner): Option<blast_admin::delayed::Proposal<u64>>

/// Whether `apply_share` would succeed now: a share is proposed, its ready time has passed, and
/// the fixed delay still fits in a Unix millisecond timestamp.
public fun is_share_ready(self: &Partner, clock: &Clock): bool

/// The ID of the applied cap, the only one that may set the recipient.
public fun cap_id(self: &Partner): ID

/// The proposed managing cap's ID with its ready time, if any. It changes nothing until applied.
public fun pending_cap_id(self: &Partner): Option<blast_admin::delayed::Proposal<ID>>

/// Whether `apply_cap` would succeed now: a cap is proposed, its ready time has passed, and the
/// fixed delay still fits in a Unix millisecond timestamp.
public fun is_cap_ready(self: &Partner, clock: &Clock): bool
```

#### Events

```move
/// Emitted at registration and on every recipient change: the partner's recipient.
/// Its share and cap events are `blast_admin::delayed`'s, owned by `partner_id`.
public struct PartnerUpdated has copy, drop {
    partner_id: ID,
    recipient: address,
}

/// Emitted whenever a partner is paid: `amount` of `T` sent to its recipient.
public struct PartnerPaid<phantom T> has copy, drop {
    partner_id: ID,
    amount: u64,
}
```

#### Constants

- `PARTNER_CHANGE_DELAY_MS: u64 = 7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1_000`: The fixed delay before a share or a cap Blast proposes can apply, and how long a partner a `partner_list::PartnerList` removes stays accepted.
- `MAX_SHARE_BPS: u64 = 8_000`: The largest share of Blast's fee one partner may earn: 80%.
- `BASIS_POINTS: u64 = 10_000`: Basis points in one whole.

### `blast_partners::partner_list`

The partners one Blast product accepts, one list per product.  A product embeds a `PartnerList` in the object holding its policy and alone decides who may change it: the list has `store` and no authority of its own, so only the embedding module can reach it mutably. Adding a partner accepts it at once. Removing one keeps it accepted for the fixed delay Blast gives for every change to a partner, `blast_partners::delay_ms()`, so anything built to name it keeps working that long. Sales and trades that already name a removed partner keep paying it; the list only gates naming it anew. Destroying the list ends every acceptance at once, without the delay, so a product destroys it only with the object that embeds it.

Source: https://github.com/interest-protocol/blast-v2-contracts/blob/main/sui/partners/sources/partner_list.move

#### Types

```move
/// The partners one product accepts: each partner's ID maps to the time, in Unix epoch
/// milliseconds, it stops being accepted, `u64::MAX` until the product removes it. `owner` is the
/// object that embeds the list, named by its events.
public struct PartnerList has store {
    owner: ID,
    acceptance_ends_at_ms: Table<ID, u64>,
}
```

#### Functions

```move
/// An empty list embedded in `owner`.
public fun new(owner: &UID, ctx: &mut TxContext): PartnerList

/// Accepts `partner` at once. Adding a partner whose removal is pending cancels the removal;
/// adding a removed partner accepts it again. Aborts when it is already accepted with no removal
/// pending.
public fun add(self: &mut PartnerList, partner: &blast_partners::Partner)

/// Stops accepting `partner_id` once the fixed delay, `blast_partners::delay_ms()`, has passed
/// from now. Aborts unless the partner is accepted now with no removal pending.
public fun remove(self: &mut PartnerList, partner_id: ID, clock: &Clock)

/// Aborts unless the list accepts `partner_id` now: it was added, and any removal's delay has
/// not yet passed.
public fun assert_accepted(self: &PartnerList, partner_id: ID, clock: &Clock)

/// Deletes the list and every entry, accepted or removed, and emits `PartnerListDestroyed`. The
/// embedding module alone holds the list by value, so it alone decides when its acceptance ends.
public fun destroy(self: PartnerList)

/// Whether the list accepts `partner_id` now; `assert_accepted` aborts exactly when this is false.
public fun is_accepted(self: &PartnerList, partner_id: ID, clock: &Clock): bool

/// Whether the list has an entry for `partner_id`: accepted, removal pending, or removed.
public fun contains(self: &PartnerList, partner_id: ID): bool

/// When the list stops accepting `partner_id`, in Unix epoch milliseconds and exclusive:
/// `u64::MAX` until removed. Aborts in `sui::dynamic_field` unless the list `contains` it.
public fun acceptance_ends_at_ms(self: &PartnerList, partner_id: ID): u64

/// The number of entries, removed partners included.
public fun length(self: &PartnerList): u64

/// The object that embeds the list, named by its events.
public fun owner(self: &PartnerList): ID
```

#### Events

```move
/// The owner's list accepts the partner from now on.
public struct PartnerAdded has copy, drop {
    owner: ID,
    partner_id: ID,
}

/// The owner's list accepts the partner until `acceptance_ends_at_ms` (Unix epoch milliseconds),
/// exclusive.
public struct PartnerRemoved has copy, drop {
    owner: ID,
    partner_id: ID,
    acceptance_ends_at_ms: u64,
}

/// The owner's list was deleted: it accepts no partner from now on.
public struct PartnerListDestroyed has copy, drop {
    owner: ID,
}
```

## API reference: `blast_boosts_core` (Boosts core)

Live on mainnet, published from an earlier revision. The source documented here has changed since; until it is republished, confirm signatures against the live package.

Events: payload structs are emitted directly, each under its own type.

Abort codes: this package aborts with the numeric codes below from whichever module detects the failure; the abort location names that module.

| Code | Constant | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | `EZeroAmount` | A fee calculation requires a positive atomic collateral amount. |
| 1 | `EInvalidFeeBps` | A fee rate must be below the full basis-point denominator. |
| 2 | `EInvalidNav` | A priced operation requires positive shareholder NAV. |
| 3 | `EInvalidShareSupply` | A priced operation requires positive share supply. |
| 4 | `EInvalidShareAmount` | Presented shares must be positive and below the live supply. |
| 5 | `ENonpositiveContribution` | A mint requires a positive shareholder NAV contribution. |
| 6 | `EZeroSharesOut` | A positive credited contribution rounded down to zero shares. |
| 7 | `ENonpositiveGross` | Post-unwind NAV does not exceed the equity kept for remaining shares. |
| 8 | `EZeroNetPayout` | The redemption fee consumed the complete gross claim. |
| 9 | `EInvalidTargetLeverageBps` | A target leverage rate must be positive. |
| 10 | `EInvalidLotSize` | A venue lot size must be positive. |
| 11 | `EInvalidBase` | A proportional mint requires positive pre-mint absolute base. |
| 12 | `EOrderBelowMinLots` | A proportional mint or redemption order is below the required minimum lot multiple. |
| 13 | `ERedemptionUnderReduced` | The final absolute base exceeds the proportional remaining base. |
| 14 | `ERedemptionOverReduced` | The final absolute base is more than one lot below the proportional remaining base without reaching flat. |
| 15 | `EArithmeticOverflow` | An arithmetic result exceeds the supported u64 range. |
| 16 | `EMaintenanceReserveExceedsEquity` | The maintenance reserve exceeds the venue equity that backs it. |
| 17 | `EInvalidLifecycleTransition` | The lifecycle cannot make the requested transition. |
| 18 | `EOperationNotPermittedInLifecycle` | The lifecycle does not permit the requested operation. |
| 19 | `EMintBaseAboveBound` | The final absolute base exceeds the pre-mint base plus the planned proportional order. |
| 20 | `EMintBaseBelowBound` | The final absolute base is below the pre-mint base plus the proportional order funded by the actual credited contribution. |
| 21 | `EInvalidMinOrderLots` | A minimum lot multiple is invalid: policy requires 2 to 1,000,000; raw arithmetic requires a positive value. |
| 22 | `EInvalidRebalancePolicy` | Rebalance thresholds are not strictly ordered. |
| 23 | `EInvalidNavCap` | A NAV cap must be positive and admit a target notional at max leverage. |
| 24 | `EInvalidMaxPriceAge` | A price maximum age must be positive. |
| 25 | `EInvalidMaxConfidenceBps` | A confidence bound must be below the basis-point denominator. |
| 26 | `EInvalidMaxMarkDivergenceBps` | A mark-divergence bound must be below the basis-point denominator. |
| 27 | `EStalePrice` | A price is older than its freshness budget. |
| 28 | `EFuturePrice` | A price is too far ahead of the reference time. |
| 29 | `EInvalidPrice` | A price used for pricing or gating is zero. |
| 30 | `EConfidenceExceedsBound` | Confidence exceeds its relative bound. |
| 31 | `EMarkOracleDivergenceExceedsBound` | Venue mark diverges too far from its oracle. |
| 32 | `EInvalidMaxSlippageBps` | Strict max slippage must be below the basis-point denominator. |
| 33 | `EInvalidEmergencyMaxSlippageBps` | Emergency slippage must include max slippage and remain below the denominator. |
| 34 | `EInvalidMinLeverageImprovementBps` | Minimum leverage improvement must be positive. |
| 35 | `ESharesOutBelowMinimum` | A mint produced fewer shares than the caller's stated minimum. |
| 36 | `ENavCapExceeded` | Shareholder NAV exceeds the Vault NAV cap. |
| 37 | `EExecutionOutsideMaxSlippage` | An executed value diverges from its reference beyond the max slippage. |
| 38 | `EInvalidFreshnessWindow` | Forward clock skew must not exceed the staleness budget. |
| 39 | `EInvalidMaxOrderNotional` | The maximum order notional must be positive. |
| 40 | `EMaxOrderNotionalUnchanged` | A maximum-order-notional update repeated the current setting. |
| 41 | `EInvalidObservationLotSize` | A normalized position observation must use a positive venue lot size. |
| 42 | `EInvalidPositionObservation` | A normalized position must be flat or use positive, lot-aligned base and notional. |
| 43 | `EOrderNotionalExceedsMaximum` | An order exceeds the live per-order maximum notional. |
| 44 | `EInvalidInitializationObservation` | A seed observation's position side differs from the immutable product side. |
| 45 | `EInitializationLeverageUnhealthy` | Seed activation leverage lies outside the immutable healthy band. |
| 46 | `EInitializationBaseBelowMinOrder` | Seed activation position cannot support the immutable minimum operation. |
| 47 | `EFeeCapExceeded` | A live fee or allocation exceeds its immutable issuance ceiling. |
| 48 | `EFeeSettingsUnchanged` | A fee update must change at least one live setting. |
| 49 | `EMintOutsideRebalanceBand` | Leverage before or after a mint lies outside the rebalance band. |
| 50 | `EActiveCheckpointChanged` | The observation pair changed between plan and completion. |
| 51 | `EActiveFillIncomplete` | The venue fill does not match the planned base order. |
| 52 | `EActiveLeverageAboveCap` | Post-operation leverage exceeds the policy maximum. |
| 53 | `ERedemptionOutputBelowMinimum` | The redemption pays less than the holder's stated minimum. |
| 54 | `ERebalanceInsideBand` | An active rebalance was requested at or inside the one rebalance band. |
| 55 | `ERebalanceNoProgress` | No admissible whole-lot rebalance progress was completed. |
| 56 | `EVenueFeeUnusable` | A venue fee or execution bound cannot be represented conservatively. |
| 57 | `EInvalidAssetDecimals` | An asset precision exceeds the widest the notional formulas support. |
| 58 | `ENavCapUnchanged` | A NAV cap update must change the cap. |
| 59 | `EInvalidMaxReserveBps` | The reserve ceiling must be a positive share of notional, at most 100%. |
| 60 | `ESeedReserveAboveCap` | A seed reserve exceeds the policy ceiling for the opening notional. |
| 61 | `EInvariantViolated` | A mutation left the state in violation of an accounting invariant that must hold by construction. |
| 62 | `EInvalidTickSize` | A venue tick size must be positive to price a limit order. |
| 63 | `EOrderCapBelowMinimum` | The live order cap cannot fund the required minimum whole-lot order. |
| 64 | `EProfitRealizationNotNeeded` | No positive cash shortfall and realizable profit require maintenance. |
| 65 | `EProfitRealizationUneconomic` | Profit realization cannot justify its bounded trading cost. |
| 66 | `EInitialMarginHeadroom` | The live venue's initial-margin settings leave no conservative opening cushion. |
| 67 | `ERebalanceNotActionable` | No whole-lot maintenance order fits its leverage and reserve constraints. |
| 68 | `ERebalanceOutsideBand` | The exceptional one-lot rebalance did not finish inside both band edges. |
| 69 | `ERebalanceCapacity` | The required improvement exceeds even a cost-free full rebalance at the NAV cap. |
| 70 | `ERebalanceOrderLimit` | A rebalance cannot accept more fills than its core-owned order budget. |
| 71 | `EProtectedShutdownNotAllowed` | The maximum circulating-share redemption is not locked by its minimum size. |
| 72 | `ERebalanceOrderMismatch` | A rebalance order's direction or emergency status differs from its plan. |

### `blast_boosts_core::blast_boosts_core`

Boosts administration roles in the shared Blast ACL, used by every leverage adapter.  A role is a type. An `AdminCap` holding `Role` signs in to `AdminWitness<Role>`, and a function's witness parameter names the one role it accepts, so a role from any other package is a different type and cannot reach these operations.  The core package is published immutably, so `UpgradeAdmin` governs adapter package custody rather than any transition in this package.

Source: https://github.com/interest-protocol/blast-v2-contracts/blob/main/sui/boosts/core/sources/blast_boosts_core.move

#### Types

```move
/// Issues an adapter Vault and its share currency, and updates that currency's metadata.
public struct VaultIssuer {}

/// Sets a Vault's fees, NAV cap and maximum order notional, and withdraws its admin fees.
public struct RiskAdmin {}

/// Irreversibly begins a Vault's shutdown.
public struct ShutdownAdmin {}

/// Authorizes and activates adapter upgrades, or permanently ends them.
public struct UpgradeAdmin {}
```

### `blast_boosts_core::constants`

Package-wide immutable core numeric constants.

Source: https://github.com/interest-protocol/blast-v2-contracts/blob/main/sui/boosts/core/sources/lib/constants.move

#### Constants

- `basis_points_denominator: u64 = 10_000`: Returns the denominator for one basis-point rate.
- `leverage_ceiling_bps: u64 = 100 * basis_points_denominator!()`: Structural ceiling on any leverage threshold: 100x in leverage basis points.  No leveraged coin in this protocol targets more than a small multiple, and the mint-contribution allowance scales with target leverage, so an unbounded threshold would let a transposed or mistyped policy admit almost any contribution. The ceiling is a sanity fence, not a selected product value.
- `max_min_order_lots: u64 = 1_000_000`: Structural ceiling on the minimum operation size in live venue lots.  The minimum exists so a small holder can still exit; a million lots can never be small in collateral terms. The fence also catches a policy that swaps `min_order_lots` with an atomic-collateral value such as the NAV cap, which would otherwise brick every mint of an immutable policy.
- `max_asset_decimals: u8 = 18`: Widest asset precision the notional formulas support without overflow.
- `max_rebalance_orders: u64 = 16`: One rebalance's bounded execution and capacity projection share this budget.
- `unwind_bound_widening_duration_ms: u64 = 86_400_000`: How long after shutdown begins the close-only execution bound takes to widen, linearly, from the ordinary bound to the emergency one: 24 hours.  A permissionless close must stay as cheap for holders as honest depth allows, yet a book that stays thin must not refuse the exit forever, so the admitted execution widens with time instead of opening at the wide bound.

### `blast_boosts_core::lifecycle`

Irreversible lifecycle and operation permissions for one Vault.

Source: https://github.com/interest-protocol/blast-v2-contracts/blob/main/sui/boosts/core/sources/lifecycle.move

#### Types

```move
/// A Vault is born active; authorized shutdown or a proven size lock moves it forward.
public enum Lifecycle has drop, store {
    Active,
    /// Shutdown began at the recorded adapter clock time; the close-only
    /// execution bound widens from that instant.
    Unwinding {
        began_at_ms: u64,
        protect_balances: bool,
    },
    Settled,
}

/// Administrator-declared operational reason, never an on-chain liquidation verdict.
public enum ShutdownReason has copy, drop {
    Emergency,
    ObservedVenueChange,
}
```

#### Functions

```move
/// Declares an administrator's emergency decision, without an objective venue verdict.
public fun emergency_reason(): ShutdownReason

/// Declares an off-chain venue-change observation, including liquidation or ADL.
public fun observed_venue_change_reason(): ShutdownReason
```

### `blast_boosts_core::observation`

Operation-scoped observations supplied by a venue adapter.  These values prove neither source identity nor caller authority. The adapter authenticates its venue and oracle sources before it constructs them; the core reads them during the enclosing operation and never stores one.

Source: https://github.com/interest-protocol/blast-v2-contracts/blob/main/sui/boosts/core/sources/observation.move

#### Types

```move
/// One normalized price and its source confidence and publication time.
///
/// Constructors require a positive price for priced operations.
public struct PriceObservation has drop {
    price: u64,
    confidence: u64,
    publish_time_ms: u64,
}

/// The external facts one operation prices against: the venue position and
/// the oracle pair, as the adapter authenticated them.
///
/// The adapter authenticates venue state and applies opening-margin admission
/// only where the operation requires it; the core values what it is given.
public struct PositionObservation has drop {
    venue_equity: u64,
    /// Unsigned position size in base-asset atoms; direction is `observed_side`.
    position_base: u64,
    lot_size: u64,
    observed_side: policy::PositionSide,
    base_oracle: PriceObservation,
    collateral_oracle: PriceObservation,
    mark_price: u64,
}

/// The normalized result of one isolated funding settlement.
public enum FundingSettlement has drop {
    Credit(u64),
    Cost(u64),
}
```

#### Functions

```move
/// Creates one positive normalized price observation.
public fun new_price(price: u64, confidence: u64, price_published_at_ms: u64): PriceObservation

/// Creates one position observation; base is whole lots and the mark is positive.
///
/// `observed_side` retains the venue's direction; it has no meaning while flat.
public fun new_position(
    venue_equity: u64,
    position_base: u64,
    lot_size: u64,
    observed_side: policy::PositionSide,
    base_oracle: PriceObservation,
    collateral_oracle: PriceObservation,
    mark_price: u64,
): PositionObservation

/// Creates a credit funding outcome.
public fun funding_credit(amount: u64): FundingSettlement

/// Creates a cost funding outcome.
public fun funding_cost(amount: u64): FundingSettlement
```

### `blast_boosts_core::policy`

Immutable core policy values and pure policy gates.  This slice selects no production value, authenticates no price source, and owns no Vault or venue state.

Source: https://github.com/interest-protocol/blast-v2-contracts/blob/main/sui/boosts/core/sources/policy.move

#### Types

```move
/// Immutable venue position direction.
///
/// Contract code uses Long and Short. Bull and Bear remain display names only.
public enum PositionSide has copy, drop, store {
    Long,
    Short,
}

/// Immutable rebalance thresholds and execution constraints for one Vault.
///
/// Values use leverage basis points, where 10,000 means 1x. Construction
/// validates only relationships that are independent of simulation; this
/// module does not select production values.
public struct RebalancePolicy has copy, drop, store {
    rebalance_below_bps: u64,
    target_leverage_bps: u64,
    rebalance_above_bps: u64,
    max_leverage_bps: u64,
    max_slippage_bps: u64,
    emergency_max_slippage_bps: u64,
    min_leverage_improvement_bps: u64,
}

/// The execution bound one venue order is priced and proved under, in basis
/// points of the reference price: the limit the adapter places the order at
/// sits inside it, and the fill must land inside it.
///
/// Only this module constructs one, from the policy's own bounds, so no
/// caller of a permissionless operation can choose the price it accepts.
public struct ExecutionBound has copy, drop {
    slippage_bps: u64,
}

/// Locally validated bounds for the price gates of one Vault.
///
/// Millisecond bounds use the on-chain clock scale. Relative bounds use the
/// package's 10,000 basis-point denominator. A future core transition will
/// verify the bound oracle source directly; the adapter owns venue observations.
/// Freshness and confidence gate each share-pricing source; mark divergence gates venue
/// margin safety only and never supplies shareholder-NAV or accounting inputs.
/// Every bound is inclusive, freshness arithmetic branches to avoid underflow,
/// and relative comparisons cross-multiply through `u128`.
///
/// This value cannot prove that observations came from the bound source or one
/// operation-scoped price pair. Those remain core and adapter obligations.
public struct PricePolicy has copy, drop, store {
    max_price_age_ms: u64,
    max_price_ahead_ms: u64,
    max_confidence_bps: u64,
    max_mark_divergence_bps: u64,
}

/// The immutable rule-set one Vault is issued with.
///
/// Fee rates are the values the Vault starts with; the admin may move them
/// later inside the caps recorded here.
public struct VaultPolicy has copy, drop, store {
    side: PositionSide,
    rebalance_policy: RebalancePolicy,
    price_policy: PricePolicy,
    /// Fee rates the Vault starts with; `State` holds the live, adjustable rates.
    initial_mint_fee_bps: u64,
    initial_redeem_fee_bps: u64,
    mint_fee_cap_bps: u64,
    redeem_fee_cap_bps: u64,
    admin_share_cap_bps: u64,
    min_order_lots: u64,
    /// Ceiling on the maintenance reserve as basis points of position notional.
    max_reserve_bps: u64,
}
```

#### Functions

```move
/// Returns the long position direction.
public fun long(): PositionSide

/// Returns the short position direction.
public fun short(): PositionSide

/// Creates one immutable rebalance policy from structurally valid values.
///
/// Thresholds must satisfy `rebalance_below < target < rebalance_above < max_leverage`,
/// and max leverage must not exceed the
/// structural `leverage_ceiling_bps` ceiling, which bounds every threshold below
/// it and so bounds the mint-contribution allowance. A zero rebalance-below
/// threshold is valid and means no caller may rebalance from below; leverage
/// can never be below zero, so the lower public trigger is then unreachable by
/// design. Max slippage must stay below 10,000 bps. Emergency max slippage
/// must be at least max slippage and below 10,000 bps. Minimum leverage improvement
/// must be positive.
public fun new_rebalance_policy(
    rebalance_below_bps: u64,
    target_leverage_bps: u64,
    rebalance_above_bps: u64,
    max_leverage_bps: u64,
    max_slippage_bps: u64,
    emergency_max_slippage_bps: u64,
    min_leverage_improvement_bps: u64,
): RebalancePolicy

/// Creates immutable price policy from proposed structural bounds.
///
/// `max_price_age_duration_ms` must be positive because the structural policy requires
/// a nonzero historical-age slippage. This check alone does not prove that a
/// selected value supports the deployed source cadence; that remains a live
/// integration and simulation gate. `max_price_ahead_duration_ms` may be zero; zero is
/// the strictest clock-skew policy and rejects the first millisecond after the
/// reference time. It must not exceed `max_price_age_duration_ms`: clock skew is never
/// larger than a staleness budget, and the rule catches a transposed pair
/// that would otherwise reject every aged update and admit future-dated ones.
///
/// Both relative bounds may be zero, which demands an exact price and an exact
/// mark, and both must stay below the 10,000 basis-point denominator. At or
/// above the denominator a confidence interval may span the complete price and
/// a divergence bound admits a zero mark, so the gate would stop constraining
/// the observation at all.
///
/// No upper millisecond bound is structural. The deployed source cadence,
/// keeper latency, venue margin parameters, and simulation select every value
/// here; this package compiles none of them and validates no value against
/// live venue state.
public fun new_price_policy(
    max_price_age_duration_ms: u64,
    max_price_ahead_duration_ms: u64,
    max_confidence_bps: u64,
    max_mark_divergence_bps: u64,
): PricePolicy

/// Composes one complete immutable policy for one future Vault.
///
/// The initial fee rates seed the live `State` rates; each stays at or below
/// its cap, and both caps stay below 10,000 bps. `admin_share_cap_bps` bounds
/// the share of future collected fees the admin may take and may equal
/// 10,000; the Vault starts with an admin share of zero.
/// `min_order_lots` is at least two and at most `max_min_order_lots`.
/// Two only excludes the vacuous one-lot rounding bound; each product still
/// needs a simulated minimum for its band, seed and intended growth.
/// `max_reserve_bps` is positive and at most 10,000: the maintenance reserve
/// may hold at most that share of position notional, and every reserve
/// credit is clamped to it so the excess stays with holders as NAV.
/// The NAV cap is not part of the policy: it is a live `State` value the
/// admin may move, supplied to `state::issue` directly.
public fun new_vault_policy(
    side: PositionSide,
    rebalance_policy: RebalancePolicy,
    price_policy: PricePolicy,
    initial_mint_fee_bps: u64,
    initial_redeem_fee_bps: u64,
    mint_fee_cap_bps: u64,
    redeem_fee_cap_bps: u64,
    admin_share_cap_bps: u64,
    min_order_lots: u64,
    max_reserve_bps: u64,
): VaultPolicy

/// The bound in basis points of the reference price.
public fun slippage_bps(self: &ExecutionBound): u64

/// The price limit an order under this bound is placed with: the reference
/// moved by the bound against the order, up for a bid and down for an ask,
/// then rounded to a multiple of `tick_size` back toward the reference.
///
/// The limit always stays inside the bound, so a venue that honors it cannot
/// fill outside the bound, and the fill proof against the same reference
/// cannot then fail on price. A tick wider than the bound leaves no such
/// price and aborts; a zero reference or tick aborts first.
public fun limit_price(
    self: &ExecutionBound,
    reference_price: u64,
    is_ask: bool,
    tick_size: u64,
): u64

/// Rejects a price outside this bound of the reference; a zero reference
/// price aborts first. Inclusive:
/// `|executed_price - reference_price| * 10_000 <= slippage_bps * reference_price`.
public fun assert_execution(self: &ExecutionBound, reference_price: u64, executed_price: u64)
```

### `blast_boosts_core::state`

Venue-neutral state for one core leveraged product.  The selected adapter stores this value inside its own shared Vault. Only functions in this module can inspect or change the private core fields. Currency, venue custody, ACL routing, and versioning belong to the adapter. The core reads no clock: every `now_ms` is the adapter's `Clock::timestamp_ms()` for the transaction, and oracle freshness is judged against it.

Source: https://github.com/interest-protocol/blast-v2-contracts/blob/main/sui/boosts/core/sources/state.move

#### Types

```move
/// An issued product before its seed position exists: the immutable policy
/// and the two live knobs the issuer set.
///
/// The adapter opens the seed position under these terms, then `activate`
/// turns them and the seeded observation into the `State`. The value has no
/// abilities, so an issuance that is not activated cannot be stored: a
/// product is either live or never existed.
public struct Issuance<phantom Product> {
    vault_policy: policy::VaultPolicy,
    max_order_notional: u64,
    nav_cap: u64,
    /// `10^decimals` of the venue's base asset and of the bound collateral:
    /// facts about the assets, fixed here so the seed orders and the live
    /// state price base the same way.
    base_unit: u64,
    collateral_unit: u64,
}

/// Sealed core state stored inside one adapter-owned Vault.
///
/// The value can be stored but cannot be copied or dropped. `Product`
/// separates independent leveraged products at the type level.
public struct State<phantom Product> has store {
    vault_policy: policy::VaultPolicy,
    /// Largest atomic-collateral notional of one adapter order, adjustable by
    /// the selected risk module. Execution slippage is bounded separately by
    /// the immutable rebalance policy, so this value only paces orders.
    max_order_notional: u64,
    /// Recorded collateral buffer inside the venue account. Mint, redemption
    /// and donation credits clamp at their observation; funding can leave an
    /// excess. Priced operations admit the live ceiling (flat positions keep all).
    maintenance_reserve: u64,
    /// Funding cost holders bore while the reserve was exhausted; later credits
    /// repay it to NAV before any credit rebuilds the reserve.
    uncovered_deficit: u64,
    /// `10^decimals` of the venue's base asset, fixed at initialization.
    base_unit: u64,
    /// `10^decimals` of the bound collateral, fixed at initialization.
    collateral_unit: u64,
    lifecycle: lifecycle::Lifecycle,
    mint_fee_bps: u64,
    redeem_fee_bps: u64,
    admin_share_bps: u64,
    /// Inclusive ceiling on post-mint shareholder NAV, adjustable by the admin.
    /// Only mints check it: NAV may exceed it through position profit, which
    /// just blocks further mints until NAV falls back under or the cap is raised.
    nav_cap: u64,
}

/// The position priced at one oracle pair: equity, base, base valued at the
/// pair, the lot, and the pair itself. Sealed into every plan and reported
/// back to the adapter; never persisted as a second ledger.
public struct ActivePosition has copy, drop {
    equity: u64,
    base: u64,
    notional: u64,
    lot_size: u64,
    base_price: u64,
    collateral_price: u64,
}

/// Linear, transaction-local mint terms. Only State can construct or finish them.
public struct MintPlan<phantom Product> {
    before: ActivePosition,
    expected_contribution: u64,
    reserve_fee: u64,
    admin_fee: u64,
    total_share_supply: u64,
    minimum_shares: u64,
    base_to_buy: u64,
    /// Only a below-band position with no executable standalone increase qualifies.
    recovery: bool,
}

/// Linear terms for one proportional redemption, before any payout or fee credit.
public struct RedemptionPlan<phantom Product> {
    before: ActivePosition,
    shares_to_redeem: u64,
    total_share_supply: u64,
    minimum_collateral_out: u64,
    fee_bps: u64,
    admin_share_bps: u64,
    base_to_sell: u64,
}

/// Linear maintenance intent, advanced only by accepted fixed-pair fills.
public struct RebalancePlan<phantom Product> {
    before: ActivePosition,
    current: ActivePosition,
    /// Opening reserve for before-progress NAV; later positions admit their own reserve.
    reserve_priced: u64,
    increase: bool,
    /// Whether the plan began above the hard cap and so may use the emergency
    /// execution bound. Such a reduction sizes toward the cap and stops when
    /// actual leverage reaches it. A later plan gets fresh admission; only
    /// ordinary bounds apply if that plan starts at or below the cap.
    emergency: bool,
    venue_fee_bps: u64,
    steps: u64,
    /// Every ordinary reduction fill matched its order and fresh core sizing.
    full_fills: bool,
    /// The last accepted increase used the sealed one-lot band exception.
    band_landing: bool,
}

/// The next whole-lot order a rebalance places: its size, direction, whether
/// the position is still above the hard cap, and the execution bound it is
/// priced and proved under. A zero size ends the plan.
public struct RebalanceOrder has drop {
    base: u64,
    increase: bool,
    emergency: bool,
    bound: policy::ExecutionBound,
    /// A single lot may cross target only when it lands inside the full band.
    band_landing: bool,
}

/// Linear terms for one bounded close-and-reopen that realizes existing profit.
/// The final base must equal the starting base; all trading costs remain in NAV.
public struct ProfitRealizationPlan<phantom Product> {
    before: ActivePosition,
    base_to_realize: u64,
    max_cost: u64,
    reserve_priced: u64,
}
```

#### Functions

```move
/// Issues one product. The caller signs in as a Vault issuer; `nav_cap` must
/// satisfy `RebalancePolicy::assert_nav_cap_valid` and stays adjustable through
/// `set_nav_cap`. The asset decimals fix the units every base valuation of this
/// product uses.
public fun issue<Product>(
    _: &blast_admin::blast_acl::AdminWitness<blast_boosts_core::VaultIssuer>,
    vault_policy: policy::VaultPolicy,
    max_order_notional: u64,
    nav_cap: u64,
    base_decimals: u8,
    collateral_decimals: u8,
): Issuance<Product>

/// Checks live venue rates against this issuance's immutable execution and
/// leverage policy. The adapter rounds each nonnegative rate upward to bps.
public fun assert_initial_margin_headroom<Product>(
    self: &Issuance<Product>,
    initial_margin_bps: u64,
    collateral_haircut_bps: u64,
    venue_fee_bps: u64,
)

/// Sizes the opening position from a flat seed observation: the whole-lot
/// target base, the whole-lot base one order may carry, and the priced flat
/// seed whose pair and lot the orders are placed under.
///
/// Sizing only. Every guard runs in `activate` against the position actually
/// filled, in the same transaction; a copy here could not refuse a state that
/// `activate` admits.
public fun seed_terms<Product>(
    self: &Issuance<Product>,
    observation: observation::PositionObservation,
    seed_reserve: u64,
): (u64, u64, ActivePosition)

/// Turns the issuance and the observation the adapter took after the seed
/// position opened into the live state.
///
/// Returns the state, the seed's reserve-excluded shareholder NAV in atomic
/// collateral units, and the priced seed position. Every price, capacity,
/// leverage and minimum-order guard runs before the state exists.
public fun activate<Product>(
    self: Issuance<Product>,
    observation: observation::PositionObservation,
    seed_reserve: u64,
    now_at_ms: u64,
): (State<Product>, u64, ActivePosition)

/// The immutable direction every seed order takes.
public fun seed_side<Product>(self: &Issuance<Product>): policy::PositionSide

/// Rejects one seed order above the per-order notional cap.
public fun assert_seed_order_notional_allowed<Product>(
    self: &Issuance<Product>,
    order_notional: u64,
)

/// The bound every seed order is priced and proved under: the ordinary one,
/// because opening a position always increases risk.
public fun seed_execution_bound<Product>(self: &Issuance<Product>): policy::ExecutionBound

/// The immutable direction every order of this product takes.
public fun side<Product>(self: &State<Product>): policy::PositionSide

/// Whole-lot capacity under the ordinary execution bound. Closing orders may
/// use exactly one venue lot when the configured cap cannot cover one lot.
public fun max_order_base<Product>(
    self: &State<Product>,
    position: &ActivePosition,
    reduce_only: bool,
): u64

/// Checks the actual filled quote against the cap. The adapter must prove
/// the fill is reduce-only and exactly one live venue lot for the sole
/// exception; the same execution-price bound still applies to that fill.
public fun assert_order_notional_allowed<Product>(
    self: &State<Product>,
    order_notional: u64,
    filled_base: u64,
    lot_size: u64,
    reduce_only: bool,
)

/// The bound every mint, redemption and ordinary rebalance order is priced and
/// proved under. A rebalance order carries its own bound, which is the wider
/// emergency one only while the position is above the hard cap, and a
/// close-only order takes the bound `unwind_constraints` prices at.
public fun execution_bound<Product>(self: &State<Product>): policy::ExecutionBound

/// Seals proportional exposure, or deposit-funded catch-up for untradeable lot dust.
/// The adapter authenticates the observation, supply and ordinary taker fee.
/// Both paths must complete inside the band; the user's share floor is unchanged.
public fun prepare_mint<Product>(
    self: &State<Product>,
    observation: observation::PositionObservation,
    collateral_deposit: u64,
    total_share_supply: u64,
    minimum_shares: u64,
    venue_fee_bps: u64,
    now_at_ms: u64,
): MintPlan<Product>

/// Returns the entire required whole-lot increase, not caller-selected sizing.
public fun base_to_buy<Product>(self: &MintPlan<Product>): u64

/// Returns the admin cash the adapter must retain before depositing collateral.
public fun admin_fee<Product>(self: &MintPlan<Product>): u64

/// Returns the sealed input for completed adapter accounting facts.
/// The position the mint was priced against; the adapter trades at its pair and lot.
public fun mint_position<Product>(self: &MintPlan<Product>): ActivePosition

/// Completes the sealed proportional or recovery fill and credits its reserve allocation.
/// The credited contribution is capped at the deposit net of the whole fee, so
/// a favorable fill accrues to existing holders (ADR 0084 D3).
/// The returned shares are minted through the adapter's native share authority.
/// The actual final position must remain inside both inclusive band edges.
/// Returns shares, contribution, fee, admin, reserve and the two sealed rates.
public fun complete_mint<Product>(
    self: &mut State<Product>,
    plan: MintPlan<Product>,
    observation: observation::PositionObservation,
    now_at_ms: u64,
): (u64, u64, u64, u64, u64)

/// Seals a rounded-up attributable close and the redeemer's output floor.
public fun prepare_redemption<Product>(
    self: &State<Product>,
    observation: observation::PositionObservation,
    shares_to_redeem: u64,
    total_share_supply: u64,
    minimum_collateral_out: u64,
    now_at_ms: u64,
): RedemptionPlan<Product>

/// Returns the full reduce-only order amount; flat redemptions require no order.
public fun base_to_sell<Product>(self: &RedemptionPlan<Product>): u64

/// The position the redemption was priced against.
public fun redemption_position<Product>(self: &RedemptionPlan<Product>): ActivePosition

/// Shares the redeemer must burn.
public fun redemption_shares<Product>(self: &RedemptionPlan<Product>): u64

/// Computes the payout after the sell and credits the fee once, excluding admin cash.
/// The gross is capped at the proportional claim, so a favorable sell accrues
/// to the remaining holders (ADR 0084 D3).
/// Returns the user payout, the admin cash, the fee, and the fee's reserve share.
/// The adapter withdraws exactly payout plus admin cash and proves that on the checkpoint.
public fun complete_redemption<Product>(
    self: &mut State<Product>,
    plan: RedemptionPlan<Product>,
    observation: observation::PositionObservation,
    now_at_ms: u64,
): (u64, u64, u64, u64)

/// Core-owned bound shared by the adapter's loop and the progress projection.
public fun max_rebalance_orders(): u64

/// Whether an outside-band position has a sizeable order the adapter permits.
/// `increases_allowed` only filters this read-only keeper hint; real execution
/// still prepares a linear plan and rechecks the venue's opening admission.
/// Projects already-settled funding without changing reserve or deficit. Every
/// admission and sizing check uses that projected reserve and the authenticated
/// ordinary fee; lot dust or an unsafe flat close returns false.
public fun needs_rebalance<Product>(
    self: &State<Product>,
    observation: observation::PositionObservation,
    funding: observation::FundingSettlement,
    increases_allowed: bool,
    venue_fee_bps: u64,
    now_at_ms: u64,
): bool

/// Derives public maintenance intent from exact outside-band ratios, never caller orders.
public fun prepare_rebalance<Product>(
    self: &State<Product>,
    observation: observation::PositionObservation,
    venue_fee_bps: u64,
    now_at_ms: u64,
): RebalancePlan<Product>

/// The next order toward the band, sized from the position the last fill left.
///
/// A zero size ends the plan; core and adapter share the core-owned order budget. An
/// emergency reduction sizes toward the hard cap using current equity and
/// the remaining position's reserve, then stops once actual leverage reaches
/// the cap. Costs and lot rounding can require several orders. A later
/// ordinary plan uses ordinary bounds; missing fills can still abort a batch.
public fun next_rebalance_order<Product>(
    self: &State<Product>,
    plan: &RebalancePlan<Product>,
): RebalanceOrder

/// The position the rebalance was priced against.
public fun rebalance_position<Product>(self: &RebalancePlan<Product>): ActivePosition

/// Whether the plan buys toward the target rather than sells.
public fun is_increasing<Product>(self: &RebalancePlan<Product>): bool

/// Whether the authenticated starting position was strictly above the hard cap.
/// Fixed for the plan: its own fills cannot promote ordinary maintenance.
public fun is_emergency_rebalance<Product>(self: &RebalancePlan<Product>): bool

public fun order_base(self: &RebalanceOrder): u64

public fun is_increase(self: &RebalanceOrder): bool

public fun is_emergency(self: &RebalanceOrder): bool

/// The bound the order is priced and proved under.
public fun bound(self: &RebalanceOrder): policy::ExecutionBound

/// Advances the plan by one accepted whole-lot fill of `order` under the fixed oracle pair.
/// The order must agree with the plan's direction and opening emergency status;
/// the plan owns the expected base movement and applicable safety checks.
public fun accept_rebalance_fill<Product>(
    self: &State<Product>,
    plan: &mut RebalancePlan<Product>,
    order: RebalanceOrder,
    observation: observation::PositionObservation,
    filled_base: u64,
    now_at_ms: u64,
)

/// Completes holder-funded maintenance without changing reserve, supply or admin cash.
/// Returns authenticated before/after equity and base for one completed event.
public fun complete_rebalance<Product>(
    self: &State<Product>,
    plan: RebalancePlan<Product>,
): (u64, u64, u64, u64, bool)

/// Sizes a whole-lot recovery of an adapter-authenticated cash shortfall and
/// an economical rounding minimum, capped to one opening-sized order. Larger deficits need further
/// transactions. No caller selects the size, price bound or cost allowance.
public fun prepare_profit_realization<Product>(
    self: &State<Product>,
    observation: observation::PositionObservation,
    cash_shortfall: u64,
    unrealized_profit: u64,
    venue_fee_bps: u64,
    now_at_ms: u64,
): ProfitRealizationPlan<Product>

/// The fixed oracle pair and starting position used by both recovery orders.
public fun realization_position<Product>(self: &ProfitRealizationPlan<Product>): ActivePosition

/// Exact base to close and reopen in the same transaction.
public fun base_to_realize<Product>(self: &ProfitRealizationPlan<Product>): u64

/// Proves unchanged exposure, bounded actual cost and a healthy final position.
/// Does not change supply, reserve, funding deficit, fees or lifecycle.
public fun complete_profit_realization<Product>(
    self: &State<Product>,
    plan: ProfitRealizationPlan<Product>,
    observation: observation::PositionObservation,
    now_at_ms: u64,
): (u64, u64, u64, u64)

/// Applies one adapter-authenticated funding classification to the reserve.
///
/// Returns `(absorbed_by_reserve, uncovered_cost, restored_to_holders)` in
/// atomic collateral units. A cost consumes the reserve first; what it cannot
/// cover is borne by holder NAV and recorded as the uncovered deficit. A credit
/// repays that deficit first, by staying in NAV, and only its remainder
/// rebuilds the reserve. The adapter owns exact-once funding checkpoint
/// authentication; the core stores no venue cursor and never infers funding
/// from an equity change.
public fun settle_funding<Product>(
    self: &mut State<Product>,
    settlement: observation::FundingSettlement,
): (u64, u64, u64)

/// Credits an exact donation to the reserve, clamped to the ceiling, without
/// creating supply or an admin entitlement. The adapter proves the venue took
/// exactly `amount` on the raw checkpoint; the core prices the position it left.
public fun donate<Product>(
    self: &mut State<Product>,
    observation: observation::PositionObservation,
    amount: u64,
    now_at_ms: u64,
)

/// Rejects an ordinary operation outside Active, before the adapter touches the venue.
public fun assert_active<Product>(self: &State<Product>)

/// Checks a recovery observation against the same prices, side and positive
/// shareholder NAV required by ordinary operations. Recovery changes no core
/// allocation: the authenticated venue loss is reflected in the next valuation.
public fun assert_recoverable_position<Product>(
    self: &State<Product>,
    observation: observation::PositionObservation,
    now_at_ms: u64,
)

/// Rejects venue synchronization after the local cash pool has been sealed.
public fun assert_can_sync<Product>(self: &State<Product>)

/// Irreversibly stops ordinary operations. The owning adapter authenticates shutdown authority.
/// Moves the Vault to Unwinding at the adapter's clock reading `now_at_ms`,
/// from which the close-only execution bound widens.
public fun begin_shutdown<Product>(self: &mut State<Product>, now_at_ms: u64)

/// Starts protected closure only when even all circulating shares cannot
/// meet the ordinary redemption minimum. The adapter authenticates raw base,
/// lot size and native supply; no price, equity or caller-sized burn is needed.
public fun begin_protected_shutdown<Product>(
    self: &mut State<Product>,
    base: u64,
    lot_size: u64,
    total_share_supply: u64,
    locked_shares: u64,
    now_at_ms: u64,
)

/// Authorizes only close-only venue progress before finalization.
public fun assert_unwinding<Product>(self: &State<Product>)

/// Prices a close-only order, sizes the per-order cap in whole lots at that
/// price, and fixes the execution bound every close order of this step is
/// priced and proved under: the ordinary bound when shutdown has just begun,
/// widening with the time since to the emergency bound. Insolvency and the
/// reserve do not gate an exit.
public fun unwind_constraints<Product>(
    self: &State<Product>,
    base_oracle: observation::PriceObservation,
    collateral_oracle: observation::PriceObservation,
    lot_size: u64,
    now_at_ms: u64,
): (policy::PositionSide, u64, u64, u64, policy::ExecutionBound)

/// Consumes the reserve book entry only after complete local cash recovery.
/// Returns eligible supply, protected reserve cash and protected seed cash.
/// Protected closure first retains the full recorded reserve up to recovered
/// cash, then floors the circulating holders' fraction of the remainder using
/// total supply including the locked seed. The adapter must segregate both
/// protected amounts with no holder/admin withdrawal path. Admin shutdown retains its
/// original distribution. Venue losses can reduce every allocation.
public fun finalize_shutdown<Product>(
    self: &mut State<Product>,
    total_share_supply: u64,
    locked_shares: u64,
    recovered_cash: u64,
): (u64, u64, u64)

/// Rejects terminal claims before any adapter cash-field access.
public fun assert_settled<Product>(self: &State<Product>)

/// Fee-free claim against current cash and total share supply, excluding the immutable seed.
public fun shutdown_claim_quote<Product>(
    self: &State<Product>,
    recovered_cash: u64,
    total_share_supply: u64,
    locked_shares: u64,
    shares_to_claim: u64,
    minimum_collateral_out: u64,
): u64

/// Updates future fee collections under immutable issuance caps.
/// Adapter custody owns authentication; no assets or past allocations move.
public fun set_fees<Product>(
    self: &mut State<Product>,
    mint_fee_bps: u64,
    redeem_fee_bps: u64,
    admin_share_bps: u64,
): (u64, u64, u64)

/// Checks locally decidable cap inputs before an adapter reads external prices.
public fun assert_max_order_notional_update<Product>(self: &State<Product>, max_order_notional: u64)

/// Updates the live per-order notional cap.
///
/// The cap uses collateral atoms and does not limit total open exposure.
/// An exact one-lot reduce-only fill may exceed it; price checks still apply.
/// Adapter custody of `State<Product>` determines who can present mutable
/// access. The adapter must authenticate its currently selected risk module
/// before calling this function. Updates are available in every lifecycle
/// state because they change only the size of later calls, not the live position.
public fun set_max_order_notional<Product>(
    self: &mut State<Product>,
    max_order_notional: u64,
    base_oracle: observation::PriceObservation,
    collateral_oracle: observation::PriceObservation,
    lot_size: u64,
    now_at_ms: u64,
): u64

/// Replaces the NAV cap and returns the previous one.
///
/// Adapter custody owns authentication. The new cap must satisfy the same
/// bound issuance applies; it may be lowered below the current NAV, which
/// only blocks further mints.
public fun set_nav_cap<Product>(self: &mut State<Product>, nav_cap: u64): u64

/// Returns the authoritative funding-only maintenance reserve.
///
/// Adapter operations use this value only for replay-complete post-state
/// events. Reserve mutation remains exclusive to core transitions.
public fun maintenance_reserve<Product>(self: &State<Product>): u64

public fun equity(self: &ActivePosition): u64

public fun base(self: &ActivePosition): u64

public fun notional(self: &ActivePosition): u64

public fun lot_size(self: &ActivePosition): u64

public fun base_price(self: &ActivePosition): u64

public fun collateral_price(self: &ActivePosition): u64
```

#### Constants

- `REBALANCE_CAPTURE_ROUNDING_ALLOWANCE: u128 = 3`: Two signed equity components and their fixed-point collateral conversion.

## API reference: `blast_boosts_products` (Boost product tags)

Live on mainnet, published from an earlier revision. The source documented here has changed since; until it is republished, confirm signatures against the live package.

Events: payload structs are emitted directly, each under its own type.

### `blast_boosts_products::blast_boosts_products`

Blast-owned product tags for Series1 Boost currencies.  A Boost currency is `blast_boost::BlastBoost<Product>` in the issuing adapter, and its `Product` argument is what a holder reads inside the coin type. Declaring every tag in this module keeps that inner type under the Blast name: `blast_boosts_products::NVDA_BULL_2X`.  Each product is one empty struct with no abilities named `<TICKER>_<SIDE>_<LEVERAGE>`, for example `public struct NVDA_BULL_2X {}`. `BULL` tracks the perp long and `BEAR` the inverse; the ticker is the Aftermath base asset without its USD suffix. A tag carries no authority and no state: Coin Registry admits one currency per tag type, and the Series1 issuer role is the only authority that can issue it. Adding a tag is a compatible upgrade of this package; nothing here is ever removed. A declared tag is not a live product until an adapter issues its currency.

Source: https://github.com/interest-protocol/blast-v2-contracts/blob/main/sui/boosts/products/sources/blast_boosts_products.move

#### Types
